**[TERM SHEET --- CONSTRUCTION-TO-MINI-PERMANENT LOAN]{.underline}**

**The Piedmont at Brightleaf** **601 and 615 Foster Street, Durham, North Carolina 27701**

**NON-BINDING EXCEPT AS SET FORTH IN SECTIONS 22 AND 23 HEREOF**

**Date:** January 10, 2025 **Bank Internal Loan Number:** CRE-2025-0342

Prepared by **Pinnacle Savings Bank, N.A.**, Commercial Real Estate Lending Division, 215 South Tryon Street, 18th Floor, Charlotte, North Carolina 28202.

This Term Sheet sets forth the proposed terms and conditions under which Pinnacle Savings Bank, N.A. (\"Lender\") is prepared to provide construction-to-mini-permanent loan financing to Harborview Capital Partners LLC (\"Borrower\") for the development of the mixed-use project known as The Piedmont at Brightleaf, located at 601 and 615 Foster Street, Durham, North Carolina 27701. Except as expressly set forth in Sections 22 and 23 hereof, this Term Sheet does not constitute a binding commitment or obligation on the part of the Lender to make the proposed Loan or on the part of the Borrower to accept the proposed Loan.

**[Section 1 --- Parties]{.underline}**

**1.1 Lender. Pinnacle Savings Bank, N.A.**, a nationally chartered savings bank organized and existing under the laws of the United States, regulated by the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency. The principal office of the Lender is located at 215 South Tryon Street, 18th Floor, Charlotte, North Carolina 28202.

**Relationship Manager:** David Forsythe, Senior Vice President, Commercial Real Estate Lending.

**Lender\'s Counsel: Ashford, Cromdale Consulting & Laine LLP, 411 South Tryon Street, Suite 2800, Charlotte, North Carolina 28202. Lead Partner: Katharine \"Kate\" Drummond. Associate: Marcus Webb.**

**1.2 Borrower. Harborview Capital Partners LLC**, a North Carolina limited liability company, organized and existing under the laws of the State of North Carolina, with the North Carolina Secretary of State File Number 1923847, formed on March 14, 2019. The principal office of the Borrower is located at 400 West Main Street, Suite 310, Durham, North Carolina 27701.

The membership interests in the Borrower are held as follows:

> • **Elena Vasquez-Torres** --- 62% membership interest (Managing Member)
>
> • **Brightleaf Investors Group LLC** --- 28% membership interest (a North Carolina limited liability company; NC Secretary of State File No. 2045612; Managing Member: Thomas R. Chen)
>

**Borrower\'s Counsel:** Calloway & Strauss PLLC, 324 Blackwell Street, Suite 200, Durham, North Carolina 27701. Lead Partner: Jonathan F. Ngo.

**1.3 Guarantors.** The following individuals shall serve as guarantors of the Loan (each, a \"Guarantor\" and collectively, the \"Guarantors\"):

> • **Elena Vasquez-Torres** --- individual, resident of Durham, North Carolina. Ms. Vasquez-Torres has approximately 22 years of commercial real estate development experience. Personal net worth: approximately \$29,800,000.

**1.4 Mezzanine Lender (Acknowledged)**

The Lender acknowledges that **Brightleaf Mezzanine Capital LLC**, a North Carolina limited liability company (NC Secretary of State File No. 2103988), will provide subordinate mezzanine financing in the amount of **\$9,200,000** in connection with the Project. The mezzanine loan shall be secured by a pledge of 100% of the membership interests in the Borrower. The mezzanine loan shall bear interest at a fixed rate of 12.50% per annum. An intercreditor agreement between the Lender and the Mezzanine Lender is currently under negotiation and must be executed prior to or simultaneously with the closing of the Loan.

**[Section 2 --- Project Description]{.underline}**

**Project Name:** The Piedmont at Brightleaf

**Property Address:** 601 and 615 Foster Street, Durham, Durham County, North Carolina 27701

**Parcel IDs:** 0821-04-72-3341 and 0821-04-72-4102

**Total Land Area:** 3.47 acres (combined two parcels)

**Zoning:** MU-D (Mixed Use --- Downtown). The proposed development is permitted as of right under the current zoning designation. No special use permit, conditional zoning, or variance is required.

**Current Condition:** Vacant improved land. The former tobacco warehouse structures on the site were demolished in August 2024. Environmental remediation of the site was completed in September 2024 in accordance with the applicable directives of the North Carolina Department of Environmental Quality (\"NCDEQ\").

**Development Description:** The Project consists of the ground-up construction of a six (6)-story (five residential stories over one podium level), Class A mixed-use residential and retail development, together with an associated structured parking garage. The development program is summarized as follows:

> • **Residential Unit Count:** 212 units, consisting of 142 one-bedroom units, 56 two-bedroom units, and 14 three-bedroom units
>
> • **Retail Space:** 18,400 square feet of ground-floor retail space across seven (7) retail bays
>
> • **Parking:** Four (4)-level structured parking garage with 276 spaces
>
> • **Total Gross Building Area:** 287,500 square feet
>
> • **Amenities:** Rooftop terrace, fitness center, co-working lounge, pool deck, and dog park

**General Contractor:** Graystone Construction Group Inc., 1200 Fayetteville Road, Raleigh, North Carolina 27603 (NC General Contractor License No. 78442; President: Mark D. Sullivan). The construction contract is a guaranteed maximum price (\"GMP\") contract with a GMP amount of **\$34,750,000**.

**Project Architect:** Meridian Design Collective PC, a North Carolina professional corporation.

**Projected Substantial Completion Date:** August 31, 2027.

**[Section 3 --- Loan Terms]{.underline}**

**3.1 Loan Amount**

**\$47,500,000** (Forty-Seven Million Five Hundred Thousand and 00/100 Dollars).

**Loan Type:** Construction-to-mini-permanent loan. The Loan shall be structured as a single advance facility, with loan proceeds to be disbursed in accordance with the approved draw schedule set forth in Section 9 of this Term Sheet.

**3.2 Loan Term**

**Construction Period:** Thirty (30) months from the date of closing. Target closing date: February 28, 2025. Construction Maturity Date: August 28, 2027.

**Mini-Perm Period:** Twelve (12) months following the Construction Maturity Date. Mini-Perm Maturity Date: August 28, 2028.

**Extension Option:** One (1) six (6)-month extension of the Mini-Perm Period (the \"Extension Option\"), resulting in an Extended Maturity Date of February 28, 2029, subject to satisfaction of customary conditions to be determined and set forth in the definitive Loan Agreement.

**3.3 Interest Rate**

**Construction Period Rate:** Daily Simple SOFR + 3.25% per annum.

**Mini-Perm Period Rate:** Daily Simple SOFR + 3.50% per annum.

**SOFR Floor:** 1.00%, applicable to both the Construction Period and the Mini-Perm Period. If Daily Simple SOFR is less than 1.00% on any applicable business day, SOFR shall be deemed to be 1.00% for purposes of calculating the interest rate applicable to such day.

**Default Rate:** The applicable contract rate plus 5.00% per annum.

Interest shall be calculated on the basis of actual days elapsed over a 360-day year. Interest on the outstanding principal balance of the Loan shall be payable monthly in arrears on the first business day of each calendar month. During the Construction Period, interest shall be funded from the Interest Reserve (as described in Section 10 hereof) until the Interest Reserve is exhausted; thereafter, interest shall be payable by the Borrower from its own funds.

\"Daily Simple SOFR\" means the Secured Overnight Financing Rate as published by the Federal Reserve Bank of New York (or a successor administrator) for the applicable business day. Benchmark replacement provisions consistent with the Alternative Reference Rates Committee\'s recommended best practices shall be included in the definitive Loan Agreement, including customary benchmark replacement triggers, successor rate identification, and spread adjustments.

**3.4 Fees. Origination Fee:** 1.00% of the Loan Amount = **\$475,000**, payable in full at closing. The origination fee may be funded from Loan proceeds in accordance with the approved Project Budget.

**Exit Fee:**

> • 0.50% of the outstanding principal balance at the time of repayment if the Loan is repaid during the Construction Period;
>
> • 0.25% of the outstanding principal balance at the time of repayment if the Loan is repaid during the first six (6) months of the Mini-Perm Period;
>
> • No exit fee shall be payable if the Loan is repaid after the first six (6) months of the Mini-Perm Period.

**Unused Line Fee:** 0.25% per annum on the average daily undrawn commitment amount, payable quarterly in arrears, commencing on the first quarterly date following closing.

**[Section 4 --- Appraisal and Valuation]{.underline}**

An appraisal of the Property has been prepared by **Ridgeline Appraisal Services Inc.** (Appraiser: Linda M. Haverford, MAI), dated November 15, 2024, and has been reviewed by the Lender\'s internal appraisal review department. The key valuation conclusions are summarized as follows:

>
> • **\"As-Completed\" Appraised Value:** \$72,800,000
>
> • **\"As-Stabilized\" Appraised Value (assumes 95% occupancy):** \$76,200,000

**Appraiser\'s Projected Stabilized Net Operating Income:**

  **Effective Gross Income**                                      **\$6,138,900**

  Less: Operating Expenses                                        (\$1,262,100)

**Implied Capitalization Rate (As-Stabilized):** 6.40%

**Loan-to-Value Ratios:**

> • LTV (As-Completed): \$47,500,000 ÷ \$72,800,000 = **65.25%**
>
> • LTV (As-Stabilized): \$47,500,000 ÷ \$76,200,000 = **62.34%**

**Projected Debt Service Coverage Ratio (Stabilized, Interest-Only):** Assuming a SOFR rate of 4.35% plus the Mini-Perm Period spread of 3.50%, the all-in interest rate would be 7.85% per annum, resulting in projected annual interest expense of approximately \$3,728,750. Based on the Appraiser\'s projected Stabilized NOI of \$4,876,800, the projected DSCR is \$4,876,800 ÷ \$3,728,750 = **1.31x**.

The Lender\'s maximum loan-to-value ratio shall not exceed 65% on an as-completed basis.

**[Section 6 --- Financial Covenants and Underwriting Requirements]{.underline}**

**6.1 Loan-to-Cost Ratio**

The maximum Loan-to-Cost Ratio shall not exceed **80%** of Total Project Costs at any time during the term of the Loan. For purposes of this Section 6.1, \"Total Project Costs\" means the aggregate of all costs and expenses incurred or to be incurred in connection with the acquisition, development, construction, and completion of the Project, as set forth in the approved Project Budget. As of the date hereof, Total Project Costs are estimated at \$56,700,000.

**6.2 Loan-to-Value Ratios**

The maximum Loan-to-Value Ratio on an as-completed basis shall not exceed **65%**. The maximum Loan-to-Value Ratio on an as-stabilized basis shall not exceed **65%**. The foregoing LTV ratios are based on the appraisal dated November 15, 2024 by Ridgeline Appraisal Services Inc. and are subject to reappraisal at any time at the Lender\'s discretion and at the Borrower\'s expense.

**6.3 Debt Service Coverage Ratio**

The minimum projected stabilized Debt Service Coverage Ratio shall be **1.25x**, based on interest-only debt service during the Mini-Perm Period. The DSCR shall be tested at the commencement of the Mini-Perm Period and annually thereafter based on actual trailing twelve-month net operating income. If at any time the DSCR falls below 1.25x, the Borrower shall, at the Lender\'s election, either (a) make a principal curtailment sufficient to restore the DSCR to 1.25x or (b) fund a cash collateral reserve in an amount determined by the Lender.

**6.4 Borrower Net Worth**

The minimum net worth of the Borrower shall be **\$12,000,000**, tested annually. The current net worth of the Borrower is approximately \$14,200,000, based on financial statements provided to the Lender.

**6.5 Guarantor Liquidity**

The minimum combined liquidity of the Guarantors shall be **\$5,000,000**, tested quarterly. Current combined guarantor liquidity is approximately \$9,300,000, consisting of approximately \$6,100,000 attributable to Elena Vasquez-Torres and approximately \$3,200,000 attributable to Reginald K. Osei. For purposes of this requirement, \"liquidity\" means cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities readily convertible to cash within thirty (30) days.

**[Section 7 --- Guaranty]{.underline}**

**7.1 Completion Guaranty**

Each Guarantor shall execute and deliver a completion guaranty (the \"Completion Guaranty\") pursuant to which each Guarantor shall jointly and severally guarantee the lien-free completion of the Project in accordance with the approved plans and specifications, the approved Project Budget, and the construction schedule, on or before the Construction Maturity Date of August 28, 2027. The Completion Guaranty shall remain in full force and effect until the Lender has received satisfactory evidence that construction of the Project has been completed in all material respects, a final certificate of occupancy has been issued by the City of Durham, and all construction liens have been released or bonded off.

**7.2 Carry Guaranty**

Each Guarantor shall execute and deliver a carry guaranty (the \"Carry Guaranty\") pursuant to which each Guarantor shall jointly and severally guarantee the payment of interest and other carrying costs on the Loan during the term of the Loan. The Carry Guaranty is in addition to, and not in lieu of, the Interest Reserve described in Section 10 hereof. The Carry Guaranty shall apply to interest and carrying costs that accrue after the Interest Reserve has been exhausted or in the event that the Interest Reserve is insufficient to cover such costs.

**7.3 Partial Repayment Guaranty**

Each Guarantor shall execute and deliver a partial repayment guaranty (the \"Partial Repayment Guaranty\") in the amount of **25% of the Loan Amount** (25% × \$47,500,000 = **\$11,875,000**). The Partial Repayment Guaranty shall be joint and several, meaning that each Guarantor shall be individually liable for the full guaranteed amount. The Partial Repayment Guaranty shall be subject to customary \"bad boy\" carve-out provisions, including but not limited to fraud, misrepresentation, voluntary bankruptcy, unauthorized transfer, environmental liability, and waste, which may convert the Partial Repayment Guaranty to a full recourse obligation. Specific carve-out triggers and the circumstances under which the partial recourse guaranty may be converted to full recourse shall be set forth in the definitive Loan Agreement.

**7.4 Environmental Indemnity**

Each Guarantor shall execute and deliver an environmental indemnity agreement (the \"Environmental Indemnity\"), unlimited in amount, indemnifying the Lender against all environmental liabilities, losses, costs, damages, and expenses (including remediation costs, fines, penalties, and attorneys\' fees) arising out of or related to the presence, release, or threatened release of any hazardous substances on, under, or from the Property. The Environmental Indemnity shall survive the repayment of the Loan, the release or reconveyance of the Deed of Trust, and any foreclosure or deed in lieu of foreclosure.

**[Section 8 --- Collateral]{.underline}**

The Loan shall be secured by the following collateral:

> • First priority Deed of Trust on the Property (Parcel IDs: 0821-04-72-3341 and 0821-04-72-4102; both parcels located at 601 and 615 Foster Street, Durham, North Carolina 27701), encumbering the fee simple interest in the Property, together with all improvements, fixtures, and appurtenances thereto;
>
> • First priority Assignment of Rents and Leases covering all current and future rents, revenues, and income from the Property;
>
> • First priority security interest in all personal property, fixtures, equipment, furniture, permits, plans, specifications, contracts, licenses, approvals, accounts, and general intangibles related to the Project;
>
> • Assignment of the construction contract (GMP contract with Graystone Construction Group Inc.), including all rights, claims, and benefits thereunder;
>
> • Assignment of the architect\'s contract (Meridian Design Collective PC), including all architectural plans, drawings, and specifications;
>
> • Collateral assignment of all insurance proceeds and condemnation awards related to the Property and the Project;
>
> • Pledge of 100% of membership interests in the Borrower by all members (Elena Vasquez-Torres --- 62%; Brightleaf Investors Group LLC --- 28%; Reginald K. Osei --- 10%);
>
> • Such other collateral as the Lender may reasonably require in connection with the Loan.

**[Section 9 --- Disbursement / Draw Schedule]{.underline}**

**9.1 General Disbursement Provisions**

Loan proceeds shall be disbursed in phases tied to construction milestones in accordance with the draw schedule set forth in Section 9.2 below. A **10% retainage holdback** shall apply to all hard construction cost disbursements. The retainage shall be held by the Lender and released only upon satisfaction of the conditions set forth below for Draw 9.

Each draw request submitted by the Borrower must be accompanied by: (a) an updated construction progress report prepared by the Borrower and the general contractor; (b) a third-party construction inspector\'s certification of the applicable milestone completion; (c) partial lien waivers from the general contractor and all subcontractors for work performed through the date of the draw request; (d) an updated title search or bring-down endorsement from Aldersgate Title & Escrow Inc. confirming the continued first-priority status of the Lender\'s Deed of Trust and the absence of any intervening liens; and (e) evidence that all insurance coverages required under Section 19 remain in full force and effect.

The Lender reserves the right to conduct independent inspections of the Property and the Project prior to authorizing each draw, at the Borrower\'s expense. The Lender shall use commercially reasonable efforts to process each draw request within ten (10) business days of receipt of a complete draw package.

**9.2 Draw Schedule**

  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Draw**          **Milestone**                                  **Cumulative % Complete**   **Amount**
  ----------------- ---------------------------------------------- --------------------------- ------------------
  1                 Closing (soft costs, interest reserve, fees)   0%                          \$9,475,000

  2                 Foundation Complete                            15%                         \$5,212,500

  3                 Structural Frame --- Level 3                   35%                         \$6,950,000

  4                 Structural Frame --- Topped Out                55%                         \$6,950,000

  5                 Building Envelope Complete                     70%                         \$5,212,500

  6                 MEP Rough-In Complete                          80%                         \$3,475,000

  7                 Interior Finish --- 50% Units                  90%                         \$3,475,000

  8                 Substantial Completion / TCO                   100%                        \$3,475,000

  9                 Retainage Release                              Post-CO                     \$3,275,000

  **Total**                                                                                    **\$47,500,000**
  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Draw 1 includes the origination fee (\$475,000), the interest reserve (\$4,850,000), and initial soft costs (\$4,150,000). The retainage release (Draw 9) is subject to receipt of a final certificate of occupancy from the City of Durham and final unconditional lien waivers from the general contractor and all subcontractors.

**[Section 10 --- Interest Reserve]{.underline}**

The Lender shall fund an interest reserve of **\$4,850,000** from Loan proceeds at closing (the \"Interest Reserve\"). The Interest Reserve shall be held in a segregated sub-account of the construction loan (the \"Interest Reserve Account\") and shall be disbursed solely for the payment of interest accruing on the outstanding principal balance of the Loan during the Construction Period. Interest payments shall be made from the Interest Reserve Account on a monthly basis in accordance with the interest payment provisions set forth in Section 3.3 hereof, until such time as the Interest Reserve is exhausted.

In the event the Interest Reserve is insufficient to cover interest payments through the end of the Construction Period, the Borrower shall be obligated to fund any shortfall from its own funds within five (5) business days of written notice from the Lender. The adequacy of the Interest Reserve shall be assessed by the Lender periodically, no less than quarterly, during the Construction Period, and the Lender shall notify the Borrower of any projected deficiency.

**[Section 11 --- Conditions Precedent to Closing]{.underline}**

The obligation of the Lender to close the Loan and make the initial advance of Loan proceeds shall be subject to the satisfaction or waiver of the following conditions precedent, each in form and substance satisfactory to the Lender and its counsel:

> • Execution and delivery of definitive Loan Documents, including but not limited to the Loan Agreement, Promissory Note, Deed of Trust, Assignment of Rents and Leases, Security Agreement, Completion Guaranty, Carry Guaranty, Partial Repayment Guaranty, Environmental Indemnity Agreement, and Pledge Agreements;
>
> • Satisfactory completion of the Lender\'s due diligence, including review of the following:
>

>
> • Phase I Environmental Site Assessment prepared by Sentinel Environmental Consulting LLC (Dr. James Whitfield, P.E.), dated October 28, 2024, and related Phase II investigation results, satisfactory to the Lender;
>
> • No Further Action letter from the North Carolina Department of Environmental Quality (\"NCDEQ\"), dated September 30, 2024, in form and substance satisfactory to the Lender;
>
> • Preliminary Title Commitment issued by Aldersgate Title & Escrow Inc. (Commitment No. NC-2024-88712, dated December 5, 2024) and issuance of a pro forma lender\'s title insurance policy in an amount not less than the Loan Amount (\$47,500,000), insuring the Lender\'s Deed of Trust as a first-priority lien on the Property, subject only to Permitted Exceptions (as defined in Section 18 hereof);
>
> • ALTA/NSPS survey satisfactory to the Lender and the title company;
>
> • Execution and delivery of the construction contract (GMP contract with Graystone Construction Group Inc.) and the architect\'s contract (Meridian Design Collective PC), in form and substance satisfactory to the Lender;
>
> • Receipt of all necessary governmental approvals, building permits, and zoning confirmations authorizing the construction and operation of the Project;
>
> • Borrower\'s organizational documents, operating agreement, certificates of good standing from the North Carolina Secretary of State, and evidence of authority (including member resolutions authorizing the Loan and all transactions contemplated hereby);
>
> • Evidence of the financial condition of the Borrower and the Guarantors, including current financial statements, personal financial statements, and federal income tax returns for the prior two taxable years;
>
> • Evidence of insurance satisfactory to the Lender, including builder\'s risk insurance (minimum \$34,750,000), commercial general liability insurance (\$5,000,000 per occurrence), and umbrella/excess liability insurance (\$10,000,000);
>
> • Payment of the origination fee in the amount of \$475,000;
>

>

>

**[Section 12 --- Representations and Warranties (Summary)]{.underline}**

The definitive Loan Agreement shall contain representations and warranties of the Borrower and the Guarantors that are customary for transactions of this type, including but not limited to the following:

> • The Borrower is duly organized, validly existing, and in good standing under the laws of the State of North Carolina and has full power and authority to own the Property, conduct its business, enter into the Loan Documents, and perform all of its obligations thereunder.
>
> • The execution, delivery, and performance of the Loan Documents have been duly authorized by all necessary action on the part of the Borrower and its members, and the Loan Documents constitute the legal, valid, and binding obligations of the Borrower, enforceable in accordance with their respective terms.
>
> • There is no litigation, proceeding, investigation, or governmental inquiry pending or, to the Borrower\'s knowledge, threatened against the Borrower, any Guarantor, or the Property that could reasonably be expected to have a material adverse effect on the Borrower, the Guarantors, the Property, or the Project.
>
> • The Property is in compliance with all applicable laws, ordinances, rules, regulations, zoning requirements, and environmental laws and regulations.
>
> • The financial statements of the Borrower and the Guarantors previously delivered to the Lender are true, complete, and accurate in all material respects and fairly present the financial condition of the Borrower and the Guarantors as of the dates thereof.
>
> • No default or event of default exists under any material agreement, instrument, or obligation to which the Borrower or any Guarantor is a party.
>
> • All permits, licenses, and approvals necessary for the construction and operation of the Project have been obtained or will be obtained prior to commencement of the applicable phase of construction.
>

**[Section 1: Executive Summary]{.underline}**

Harborview Capital Partners LLC (the \"Borrower\") has requested a \$47,500,000 construction-to-mini-permanent loan from Pinnacle Savings Bank, N.A. (the \"Bank\") for the ground-up construction of \"The Piedmont at Brightleaf,\" a 212-unit Class A mixed-use residential and retail development located at 601 and 615 Foster Street, Durham, Durham County, North Carolina 27701. The subject property comprises two parcels (Parcel IDs 0821-04-72-3341 and 0821-04-72-4102) with a combined land area of approximately 3.47 acres. The site is currently improved as vacant land, following the demolition of former tobacco warehouse structures in August 2024 and the completion of environmental remediation in September 2024.

The proposed development consists of a six-story mixed-use building with five residential floors constructed above a one-story podium containing ground-floor retail space and a four-level structured parking garage. The residential program comprises 212 units: 142 one-bedroom units, 56 two-bedroom units, and 14 three-bedroom units. Ground-floor retail consists of approximately 18,400 square feet across seven retail bays. The structured parking garage provides 276 parking spaces, representing a ratio of approximately 1.30 spaces per residential unit. Total gross building area is approximately 287,500 square feet. Project amenities include a rooftop terrace, fitness center, co-working lounge, pool deck, and dog park. The property is zoned MU-D (Mixed Use --- Downtown), and the proposed development is permitted as of right under the applicable zoning ordinance.

The Relationship Manager for this credit is David Forsythe, SVP, Commercial Real Estate Lending. A term sheet was executed on January 10, 2025 by David Forsythe on behalf of the Bank and Elena Vasquez-Torres, Managing Member of the Borrower. The target closing date is February 28, 2025. The Bank\'s outside legal counsel for this transaction is Ashford, Cromdale Consulting & Laine LLP (lead partner Katharine \"Kate\" Drummond; associate Marcus Webb), located at 411 South Tryon Street, Suite 2800, Charlotte, North Carolina 28202. The Borrower\'s counsel is Calloway & Strauss PLLC (lead partner Jonathan F. Ngo), located at 324 Blackwell Street, Suite 200, Durham, North Carolina 27701.

The Commercial Real Estate Lending group recommends **APPROVAL** of this loan, subject to material conditions including, without limitation, (a) resolution of a loan-to-cost ratio exceedance through funding of an equity escrow deposit, (b) execution of an intercreditor agreement with the mezzanine lender, (c) implementation of single-purpose entity covenants and delivery of a non-consolidation opinion, and (d) resolution of other conditions detailed in Section 10 of this memorandum. The loan as structured presents certain underwriting concerns regarding borrower equity contribution and LTC compliance that must be addressed as conditions of closing. Additionally, this credit memorandum identifies several risk factors and structural issues --- including interest reserve adequacy, affiliate relationships between a Borrower member and the mezzanine lender, conflicting membership interest pledges, environmental use restrictions, and title matters --- each of which requires resolution or mitigation before or at closing. The Borrower is Harborview Capital Partners LLC, a North Carolina limited liability company formed on March 14, 2019 and registered with the North Carolina Secretary of State under File Number 1923847. The Bank\'s underwriting standards for construction loans require standard SPE covenants, including separateness covenants, restrictions on commingling of funds with affiliates, and prohibition on incurrence of additional indebtedness outside the approved capital structure. **[3.2 Market Overview]{.underline}**

The Durham, North Carolina multifamily market continues to demonstrate strong fundamentals driven by the area\'s robust economic base. The Research Triangle region --- anchored by Duke University, the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, and North Carolina State University --- has attracted significant investment in biotechnology, pharmaceutical research, information technology, and financial services. Downtown Durham, in particular, has experienced substantial revitalization over the past decade, with the American Tobacco Campus, Durham Innovation District, and the expanding Duke University Health System serving as major employment and demand drivers. Population growth in Durham County has averaged approximately 1.8% annually over the past five years, and the median household income in the downtown core has increased by over 15% during the same period.

Average market rents for Class A multifamily product in downtown Durham currently range from approximately \$1,950 to \$2,500 per month for one-bedroom units and \$2,300 to \$3,200 per month for two-bedroom units, depending on unit size, finishes, and amenity package. The Project\'s projected average rent of \$2,245 per month across all unit types is positioned in the mid-range of the competitive set and is supported by comparable lease data from properties including the Van Alen, One City Center Apartments, and Beckon on Geer Street. The Bank considers this rent projection to be reasonable and achievable based on current market conditions.

Ground-floor retail rents in downtown Durham for Class A mixed-use buildings with street-level visibility range from approximately \$26.00 to \$35.00 per square foot on a triple-net basis. The projected retail rent of \$30.00 per square foot NNN is within this market range and is considered reasonable given the Project\'s location and visibility along Foster Street.

Durham Class A multifamily vacancy rates have historically ranged from approximately 4% to 7%, with the most recent data indicating a vacancy rate of approximately 5.2% for comparable properties. The Project\'s underwritten vacancy assumption of 5% is consistent with historical trends and is considered appropriate. While there is a notable pipeline of competing multifamily projects under development or planned in the greater Durham area, market demand continues to absorb new supply at a rate that supports the Project\'s lease-up assumptions. The Bank\'s independent market assessment supports the appraised values discussed in Section 3.3.

**The Borrower is contributing \$0 in direct cash equity to the Project.** The land acquisition cost of \$8,200,000 was funded from prior capital calls from members, including contributions from Brightleaf Investors Group LLC, which is affiliated with the mezzanine lender, Brightleaf Mezzanine Capital LLC. All remaining project costs are funded through the senior construction loan and the mezzanine loan. Per the Bank\'s underwriting policy, mezzanine debt is not counted as borrower equity.

The LTC calculation presents a compliance issue. Total project costs equal \$56,700,000. The senior loan amount is \$47,500,000. Therefore, LTC = \$47,500,000 ÷ \$56,700,000 = **83.77%**. The Bank\'s maximum permitted LTC per the executed term sheet and per the Bank\'s Commercial Real Estate Lending Policy is 80%. At the maximum LTC of 80%, the maximum permitted senior loan amount would be \$56,700,000 × 80% = \$45,360,000. The proposed loan amount of \$47,500,000 exceeds this maximum by \$2,140,000. This discrepancy must be resolved prior to closing through the equity escrow mechanism described in Section 5.3 and conditioned in Section 10.

Additionally, the Bank notes that the Borrower\'s only equity contribution to the Project is the previously acquired land, which has an as-is appraised value of \$8,900,000 and was acquired for \$8,200,000. While the land value exceeds the \$2,140,000 shortfall, a portion of the capital used to acquire the land was sourced from Brightleaf Investors Group LLC, an affiliate of the mezzanine lender. This creates a potential circular funding concern. The Senior Loan Committee requires, as a condition of closing, that the Borrower either: (a) deposit \$2,140,000 in cash into a Bank-controlled equity escrow account prior to closing; or (b) reduce the loan amount to \$45,360,000; or (c) provide additional evidence satisfactory to the Bank that the land equity is independent of the mezzanine financing.

The loan-to-cost ratio is a critical underwriting metric that measures the Bank\'s exposure relative to total project costs. The detailed LTC calculation is as follows:

The LTC ratio of 83.77% exceeds the Bank\'s maximum of 80% as stated in the term sheet. The term sheet was executed with a loan amount of \$47,500,000 and total project costs of \$56,700,000 without reconciling the LTC covenant. This discrepancy must be resolved prior to closing. The Senior Loan Committee acknowledges the LTC exceedance and approves the loan subject to the condition that the Borrower fund an equity escrow deposit of not less than \$2,140,000 in cash (from sources other than the mezzanine loan or any affiliate of the mezzanine lender) into a Bank-controlled escrow account prior to or at closing. For additional context, the Bank notes the following alternative analysis: If the mezzanine debt of \$9,200,000 were hypothetically counted as equity (which the Bank\'s underwriting policy does not permit), the combined \"equity\" in the capital structure would be \$9,200,000 and the senior loan LTC would remain unchanged at 83.77%. The combined senior and mezzanine leverage is (\$47,500,000 + \$9,200,000) ÷ \$56,700,000 = 100%, meaning there is zero true equity cushion in the capital structure absent the land value. This analysis underscores the importance of the equity escrow requirement and the need for the Bank to confirm that the land equity is genuinely independent of the mezzanine financing.

Even with the proposed equity escrow of \$2,140,000, the Borrower\'s total equity contribution to the Project would consist of \$2,140,000 in cash plus \$8,200,000 in land (at cost), totaling \$10,340,000 out of \$56,700,000 in total project costs, or approximately 18.2%. While this level of equity is relatively thin for a ground-up construction loan, the Bank takes comfort in the strong LTV ratios (65.25% as-completed, 62.34% as-stabilized) and the combined guarantor net worth of \$41,300,000 as additional credit support.

Assuming a Daily Simple SOFR rate of 4.35% (as of the credit memo date) plus the mini-perm spread of 3.50%, the all-in rate is 7.85%. Annual interest on \$47,500,000 at 7.85% = \$3,728,750. DSCR = \$4,876,800 ÷ \$3,728,750 = **1.31x**, which exceeds the Bank\'s minimum of 1.25x.

**Stress-Tested DSCR.** Under a stress scenario assuming a 200-basis-point increase in SOFR (to 6.35%), the all-in mini-perm rate would be 9.85% (6.35% + 3.50%). Annual interest on \$47,500,000 at 9.85% = \$4,678,750. Stressed DSCR = \$4,876,800 ÷ \$4,678,750 = **1.04x**, which falls below the Bank\'s minimum of 1.25x. This stress test illustrates the loan\'s sensitivity to interest rate increases and underscores the importance of the Borrower securing permanent take-out financing or obtaining an interest rate cap prior to the commencement of the mini-perm period or any extension thereof. The Bank should consider requiring an interest rate cap as a condition of the extension option.

**[6.2 Interest Reserve Analysis]{.underline}**

The interest reserve of \$4,850,000 is funded from loan proceeds at closing and held in a designated sub-account to cover monthly interest payments during the construction period. The adequacy of this reserve is a critical underwriting consideration, as depletion of the reserve before construction completion would require the Borrower to fund interest from its own resources.

**Current Rate Assumptions.** The current Daily Simple SOFR rate is approximately 4.35% as of the date of this memorandum. The construction period all-in rate is Daily Simple SOFR + 3.25% = 7.60%.

**Full-Draw Scenario.** If the entire \$47,500,000 were drawn immediately at closing, the annual interest expense would be \$47,500,000 × 7.60% = \$3,610,000. Over the 30-month construction period, total interest cost would be approximately \$3,610,000 × (30 ÷ 12) = \$9,025,000. However, this scenario is unrealistic because the loan is drawn incrementally over the construction period based on milestone achievements.

**Incremental Draw Scenario.** Based on the draw schedule (Section 7.1), the loan is drawn progressively as construction milestones are achieved. Draw 1 at closing (\$9,475,000) represents approximately 20% of the total loan commitment. Subsequent draws bring cumulative outstanding balances to progressively higher levels, with Draw 8 (substantial completion) bringing cumulative draws to approximately \$44,225,000 and the final Draw 9 (retainage release) occurring post-certificate of occupancy. Assuming a roughly linear draw pattern over approximately 18 months to reach the full commitment level (with the remaining 12 months of the construction period at or near full draw), the average outstanding balance over the 30-month construction period is estimated at approximately \$28,500,000 (roughly 60% of \$47,500,000).

Using this average balance, the estimated total interest cost during the 30-month construction period is: \$28,500,000 × 7.60% × (30 ÷ 12) = approximately **\$5,415,000**.

The interest reserve of \$4,850,000 is therefore approximately **\$565,000 short** of the estimated total interest cost under current rate assumptions.

**Sensitivity Analysis.** If SOFR increases by 100 basis points to 5.35%, the all-in construction rate would be 8.60%. Estimated total interest cost would increase to \$28,500,000 × 8.60% × (30 ÷ 12) = approximately **\$6,128,000**, creating a potential shortfall of approximately \$1,278,000.

Furthermore, the draw schedule is somewhat front-loaded, with the initial closing draw of \$9,475,000 representing approximately 20% of the total commitment. This front-loading means the average outstanding balance may be higher than the linear assumption suggests, potentially increasing the total interest cost and widening the reserve shortfall.

**Assessment.** The interest reserve of \$4,850,000 is **tight** under current rate assumptions and would be clearly inadequate in a rising rate environment. The Senior Loan Committee approves the interest reserve of \$4,850,000 as adequate based on current rate assumptions, but notes that this amount is at the lower boundary of adequacy. The loan documentation must include the following protective provisions:

> • A mandatory borrower replenishment obligation requiring the Borrower to fund any interest reserve shortfall from its own funds (not from loan proceeds or mezzanine loan proceeds) upon demand by the Bank.
>
> • An interest reserve adequacy test to be performed at each draw request, comparing the remaining interest reserve balance against projected interest costs through the earlier of (a) the next anticipated draw date or (b) 90 days. If the projected costs exceed the remaining reserve balance, the Borrower must deposit additional funds into the interest reserve sub-account before the requested advance will be funded.

> • A reporting obligation requiring the Borrower to provide the Bank with a monthly reconciliation of the interest reserve balance, actual interest charges, and projected remaining interest costs through construction maturity.

**[PHASE I ENVIRONMENTAL SITE ASSESSMENT]{.underline}**

**[EXCERPTED SECTIONS]{.underline}**

**[(Findings, Conclusions, and Recommendations)]{.underline}**

**THE PIEDMONT AT BRIGHTLEAF**

**601 and 615 Foster Street** **Durham, Durham County, North Carolina 27701**

**Parcel IDs: 0821-04-72-3341 and 0821-04-72-4102**

**Prepared for:**

**Harborview Capital Partners LLC** 400 West Main Street, Suite 310 Durham, North Carolina 27701

and

**Pinnacle Savings Bank, N.A.** (as Intended Reliance Party / Lender) 200 South Tryon Street, 18th Floor Charlotte, North Carolina 28202

**Prepared by:**

**Sentinel Environmental Consulting LLC** 2700 Battleground Avenue, Suite 400 Greensboro, North Carolina 27408

**Lead Consultant:** Dr. James Whitfield, P.E. Senior Principal Environmental Scientist

**Report Date:** October 28, 2024

**Sentinel Project No.: SEC-2024-1147**

This document contains excerpted sections from the full Phase I Environmental Site Assessment report prepared by Sentinel Environmental Consulting LLC under Project No. SEC-2024-1147. The complete report, including all appendices, historical research documentation, regulatory database search results, interview records, and photographic documentation, is available under separate cover. This excerpted document is intended to provide a summary of findings, conclusions, and recommendations for the convenience of the client and the intended reliance party. It does not replace or supersede the full report and should be read in conjunction with the complete Phase I Environmental Site Assessment.

This assessment was conducted in conformance with ASTM Standard Practice E1527-21, *Standard Practice for Environmental Site Assessments: Phase I Environmental Site Assessment Process*, published by ASTM International, and in compliance with the All Appropriate Inquiries (AAI) rule codified at 40 C.F.R. Part 312.

Right-click to update Table of Contents

**[1. Executive Summary of Findings]{.underline}**

Sentinel Environmental Consulting LLC (\"Sentinel\") was retained by Harborview Capital Partners LLC (\"Harborview\" or \"Client\") to conduct a Phase I Environmental Site Assessment (\"Phase I ESA\" or \"Assessment\") of the property located at 601 and 615 Foster Street, Durham, Durham County, North Carolina 27701 (the \"Subject Property\"). The assessment was conducted for the purpose of supporting proposed financing by Pinnacle Savings Bank, N.A. (\"Pinnacle\" or \"Lender\") and to satisfy the requirements of the All Appropriate Inquiries (\"AAI\") rule under 40 C.F.R. Part 312, thereby supporting potential assertion of the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act (\"CERCLA\") innocent landowner, contiguous property owner, and bona fide prospective purchaser defenses.

The Subject Property consists of two contiguous parcels: Parcel ID 0821-04-72-3341 (approximately 1.89 acres, fronting 601 Foster Street) and Parcel ID 0821-04-72-4102 (approximately 1.58 acres, fronting 615 Foster Street), totaling approximately 3.47 acres of land. The Subject Property is situated within Durham\'s historic Brightleaf tobacco district, an area that has experienced significant redevelopment over the past two decades. The property is currently vacant improved land. Former tobacco warehouse structures that had occupied both parcels were demolished in August 2024, and environmental remediation activities were completed in September 2024. The site is graded and secured with temporary construction fencing.

The property is zoned MU-D (Mixed Use --- Downtown) by the City of Durham and is planned for development as \"The Piedmont at Brightleaf,\" a 212-unit Class A mixed-use residential and retail development. The proposed project includes 18,400 square feet of ground-floor retail space and a 276-space structured parking garage. The building is designed as a 6-story structure --- five residential levels over one podium level --- with a total gross building area of approximately 287,500 square feet. The project architect is Meridian Design Collective PC, and the general contractor is Graystone Construction Group Inc. (NC License No. 78442).

Based on the assessment conducted herein, one Recognized Environmental Condition (\"REC\") was identified at the Subject Property. The REC consists of residual petroleum contamination from a former underground storage tank (\"UST\") located in the northeast corner of Parcel 0821-04-72-4102. The former UST, a 2,000-gallon diesel fuel tank, was historically associated with a backup generator that served the tobacco warehouse operations. The REC has been subject to a Phase II Environmental Site Assessment investigation (August 2024) and subsequent remediation consisting of soil excavation and off-site disposal (September 2024). A No Further Action (\"NFA\") determination letter was issued by the North Carolina Department of Environmental Quality (\"NCDEQ\"), Inactive Hazardous Sites Branch (\"IHSB\"), on September 30, 2024, for Site ID IHSB-24-1203.

The NFA letter is conditional. It is premised upon (a) the installation of a soil vapor mitigation system beneath any enclosed structure constructed over the affected area, (b) a restriction of future use to non-residential purposes on the affected approximately 0.38-acre area in the northeast corner of Parcel 0821-04-72-4102, (c) compliance with a soil management plan for future excavation activities within the affected area, and (d) the recording of a deed notice in the Durham County Registry of Deeds within 60 days of the NFA letter date.

No other Recognized Environmental Conditions, Controlled Recognized Environmental Conditions (\"CRECs\"), or Historical Recognized Environmental Conditions (\"HRECs\") were identified during this assessment. Several de minimis conditions were noted during the site reconnaissance and are described in the full report; however, these conditions do not rise to the level of RECs under ASTM E1527-21.

**[2. Site Description and History]{.underline}**

**2.1 Physical Description**

The Subject Property is composed of two contiguous parcels at 601 Foster Street (Parcel 0821-04-72-3341, approximately 1.89 acres) and 615 Foster Street (Parcel 0821-04-72-4102, approximately 1.58 acres), located in downtown Durham, Durham County, North Carolina 27701. The combined area of the two parcels is approximately 3.47 acres. The site fronts Foster Street to the north and is bounded by commercial and mixed-use properties on the remaining sides.

The topography of the Subject Property is generally flat, with a gentle slope of approximately 2 percent from northwest to southeast. Site elevation ranges from approximately 395 feet to 401 feet above mean sea level, as confirmed by topographic survey and regional United States Geological Survey data. The site drains generally toward the southeast, consistent with the surrounding topographic gradient and the regional drainage pattern toward the Ellerbe Creek watershed.

The site is currently vacant. All former structures have been demolished and removed as of August 2024. The ground surface has been graded and the site is enclosed by temporary six-foot chain-link construction fencing with green privacy screening. Existing utility infrastructure --- including municipal water and sanitary sewer lines, electrical service, natural gas, and telecommunications conduit --- has been stubbed to the property boundaries in anticipation of the proposed development. A 20-foot utility easement runs along the western boundary of the site and is occupied by Duke Energy utility poles and overhead electrical lines. A stormwater management easement of approximately 0.22 acres, recorded in the Durham County Registry of Deeds at Book 7421, Page 212, occupies the southern portion of the site and contains a graded drainage swale and inlet structure.

**2.2 Historical Use Summary**

The historical use of the Subject Property was researched through review of Sanborn Fire Insurance Maps (1901, 1913, 1924, 1937, 1950), historical aerial photographs (1955, 1965, 1972, 1981, 1993, 2005, 2012, 2019), city directories (various years, 1910--2005), Durham County building permit records, Durham County tax records, and interviews with persons knowledgeable about the property. The following chronological summary was developed from these sources:

**1900--1965:** Both parcels were occupied by tobacco warehouses and associated processing buildings. The site was part of Durham\'s historic Brightleaf tobacco district, which was the center of the American bright-leaf tobacco industry during the early twentieth century. Sanborn maps from 1901 through 1950 depict large, multi-bay warehouse structures on both parcels, with rail siding access along the southern boundary of the property. The warehouses were used for the curing, grading, and storage of leaf tobacco, and later for the manufacture of tobacco products. These operations were consistent with the industrial character of the surrounding area during this period.

**1965--1990:** Following the decline of the Durham tobacco industry, the warehouse buildings were converted to light industrial and general commercial storage uses. City directory listings from this period indicate tenants including a furniture refinishing operation, a printing company, and a general storage and distribution business. During this period, a 2,000-gallon underground storage tank was installed on the northeast corner of Parcel 0821-04-72-4102 to store diesel fuel for a backup generator serving the warehouse operations. Based on a review of Durham County building permit records, the estimated installation date of the UST is approximately 1972. The UST was reportedly decommissioned and removed in approximately 1998; however, no formal UST closure records were located in the files of the Durham County Fire Marshal or the NCDEQ UST Section despite Sentinel\'s diligent efforts to obtain such records.

**1990--2005:** Light industrial use continued at diminishing levels. Several tenants vacated the property during the 1990s, and by the early 2000s the warehouse buildings were largely unoccupied. Aerial photographs from 1993 and 2005 show the buildings in increasingly deteriorated condition, with portions of the roofing compromised and vegetation encroaching on the southern portions of the site. Surface parking occupied portions of the unpaved areas between the buildings during this period.

**2005--2022:** The property was largely vacant, with the warehouse structures remaining in place but unoccupied. The site was used intermittently as unpaved surface parking, primarily serving visitors to the adjacent Brightleaf Historic District and American Tobacco Campus. Ownership of the parcels changed multiple times during this period, as reflected in the Durham County deed records.

**2022--Present:** Harborview Capital Partners LLC acquired the Subject Property in 2022 for the purpose of redevelopment. A pre-demolition hazardous materials survey was conducted by an independent consultant in July 2024, and demolition of the remaining warehouse structures was completed in August 2024. Environmental remediation, consisting of excavation and off-site disposal of petroleum-impacted soil in the northeast corner of Parcel 0821-04-72-4102, was completed in September 2024.

**2.3 Surrounding Land Uses and Environmental Setting**

The Subject Property is situated in a mixed commercial and entertainment district in downtown Durham. Surrounding land uses include the Brightleaf Historic District (commercial retail and restaurant uses) to the north and west, the American Tobacco Campus (mixed-use commercial, office, and entertainment development) to the south, and the Durham Performing Arts Center and associated commercial development to the east. These surrounding properties are generally developed with commercial or institutional uses and do not present obvious indicators of significant environmental concern with respect to the Subject Property.

The site is located in the Durham Triassic Basin, a geological formation characterized by interbedded sandstone, siltstone, and mudstone of the Newark Supergroup. Depth to groundwater in the vicinity of the Subject Property is estimated at approximately 15 to 25 feet below grade, based on regional hydrogeological data and measurements obtained from monitoring wells installed during the Phase II investigation. The inferred groundwater flow direction is generally to the southeast, consistent with the regional topographic gradient.

The Subject Property is not located within a Federal Emergency Management Agency (\"FEMA\") designated Special Flood Hazard Area. According to FEMA Flood Insurance Rate Map Panel 3720098700J, effective March 2, 2009, the site is located in Zone X, an area of minimal flood hazard.

**[3. Environmental Database and Regulatory Records Review]{.underline}**

A standard ASTM-required environmental database search was conducted by Environmental Data Resources, Inc. (\"EDR\") for the Subject Property and surrounding areas within the applicable ASTM search radii. The database search date was October 10, 2024, and the complete search report is attached as Appendix A to the full Phase I ESA report.

**3.1 Subject Property Listings**

The Subject Property was identified in the following regulatory databases:

**NCDEQ Incident Management Database (IMD):** The property at 615 Foster Street (Parcel 0821-04-72-4102) is listed as Site No. NONUST-24-0847 in the NCDEQ Incident Management Database. This listing relates to the petroleum contamination identified during the Phase II investigation conducted in August 2024 in connection with the former 2,000-gallon diesel UST. The incident was reported to NCDEQ on August 12, 2024, following the confirmation of contamination above applicable soil remediation goals.

**NCDEQ Inactive Hazardous Sites Branch Database:** The Subject Property is listed as Site ID IHSB-24-1203 in the NCDEQ IHSB database. The current status of this listing is \"NFA --- Conditional\" as of September 30, 2024, reflecting the issuance of the conditional No Further Action determination letter described in Section 7 of this report.

The Subject Property was not identified on the National Priorities List (\"NPL\"), the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Information System (\"CERCLIS\"), the Resource Conservation and Recovery Information System (\"RCRIS\") as either a large-quantity or small-quantity generator of hazardous waste, the North Carolina Pre-Regulatory Landfill Inventory, the North Carolina equivalent superfund list, or any other federal or state database that would indicate the presence of additional environmental conditions beyond those already identified herein.

**3.2 Adjoining and Nearby Property Listings**

The EDR database search identified several properties within the applicable ASTM search radii that are listed on various environmental databases. Specifically, three nearby properties are listed as active Leaking Underground Storage Tank (\"LUST\") sites within the one-half mile ASTM search radius. Upon review, these LUST sites are located either cross-gradient or down-gradient of the Subject Property relative to the inferred groundwater flow direction. **[5. Phase II Investigation Results (Summary)]{.underline}**

*Note: The Phase II Environmental Site Assessment referenced in this section was performed by Sentinel Environmental Consulting LLC under a separate scope of work and separate contractual engagement in August 2024. The Phase I ESA does not include sampling or analysis as part of its scope. The following summary is provided for reference and completeness in understanding the environmental conditions identified at the Subject Property. The complete Phase II investigation report is available under separate cover (Sentinel Project No. SEC-2024-1089) and is also referenced in the NCDEQ project files for Site ID IHSB-24-1203.*

**5.1 Scope of Investigation**

The Phase II investigation was conducted in August 2024 and was focused on the northeast corner of Parcel 0821-04-72-4102, in the vicinity of the former 2,000-gallon diesel underground storage tank. The investigation scope included the advancement of twelve soil borings (designated SB-01 through SB-12) to depths ranging from 15 to 25 feet below grade, the installation and sampling of three groundwater monitoring wells (designated MW-01, MW-02, and MW-03), and the collection of soil gas samples from eight sub-slab soil gas probes (designated SG-01 through SG-08) installed at a depth of approximately 5 feet below grade. All sampling and analysis were conducted in accordance with NCDEQ-approved sampling protocols, and all samples were analyzed by a North Carolina-certified analytical laboratory (Pace Analytical Services, Huntersville, North Carolina).

**5.2 Soil Analytical Results**

Total petroleum hydrocarbons in the diesel range organics (\"TPH-DRO\") fraction were detected in soil samples collected from borings within and adjacent to the former UST location at concentrations ranging from non-detect (below the laboratory method detection limit of 5.0 mg/kg) to a maximum of 847 mg/kg in soil boring SB-07 at a depth of 10 feet below grade. Benzene was detected in soil samples at a maximum concentration of 0.42 mg/kg, also in boring SB-07 at a depth of 8 feet below grade. Additional petroleum-related constituents, including toluene, ethylbenzene, and xylenes, were detected at lower concentrations in several borings within the affected area.

The lateral extent of petroleum contamination was generally limited to an area of approximately 0.38 acres in the northeast corner of Parcel 0821-04-72-4102. Borings SB-05 through SB-09, located within this area, exhibited the highest concentrations, while borings SB-01 through SB-04, SB-10, SB-11, and SB-12, located outside or at the periphery of the affected area, exhibited non-detect or trace-level concentrations. Vertically, the contamination extended from approximately 4 feet to 14 feet below grade, with the highest concentrations observed at depths of 8 to 12 feet, consistent with the inferred depth of the former UST and the surrounding backfill soils.

The detected concentrations were compared to the NCDEQ Inactive Hazardous Sites Branch Preliminary Soil Remediation Goals (\"PSRGs\") for both residential and non-residential land uses. The following table summarizes the critical comparisons:

  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Constituent**   **Maximum Detected Concentration**   **NCDEQ Residential PSRG**   **Exceeds Residential?**   **NCDEQ Non-Residential PSRG**   **Exceeds Non-Residential?**
  ----------------- ------------------------------------ ---------------------------- -------------------------- -------------------------------- ------------------------------
  TPH-DRO           847 mg/kg                            100 mg/kg                    Yes                        1,000 mg/kg                      No

  Benzene           0.42 mg/kg                           0.065 mg/kg                  Yes                        0.89 mg/kg                       No
  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

As indicated in the table above, the maximum detected concentrations of both TPH-DRO and benzene in soil exceeded the NCDEQ residential PSRGs but were below the NCDEQ non-residential (commercial/industrial) PSRGs. This distinction is significant because the NCDEQ applies different risk-based cleanup standards depending on the intended land use. The residential PSRGs are more stringent because they are designed to be protective of long-term residential exposure, including exposure to young children and other sensitive populations, under a 30-year residential exposure scenario.

**5.3 Groundwater Analytical Results**

Dissolved-phase petroleum constituents were detected in groundwater samples collected from monitoring well MW-02, which is located within the affected area in the northeast corner of Parcel 0821-04-72-4102. Specifically, dissolved benzene was detected at a concentration of 0.8 µg/L (the North Carolina 2L Groundwater Quality Standard for benzene is 1.0 µg/L) and dissolved TPH-DRO was detected at 320 µg/L. All other dissolved-phase constituents were either non-detect or detected at concentrations well below applicable 2L Standards. Monitoring wells MW-01 and MW-03, located on the periphery of the affected area, did not exhibit detectable concentrations of dissolved petroleum constituents, indicating that the dissolved-phase groundwater plume has not migrated significantly beyond the immediate vicinity of the former UST location and does not appear to have migrated off-site.

**5.4 Soil Gas Analytical Results**

Volatile organic compounds, including benzene and naphthalene, were detected in soil gas samples collected from probes within and near the affected area. The most significant soil gas detection was benzene at a concentration of 185 µg/m³ in soil gas sample SG-04, which is located within the center of the affected area. The NCDEQ residential vapor intrusion screening level for benzene in sub-slab soil gas is 31 µg/m³. The detected concentration of 185 µg/m³ exceeds this screening level by a factor of approximately six, indicating the potential for vapor intrusion into enclosed structures constructed over the affected area. Naphthalene was also detected in soil gas samples SG-03, SG-04, and SG-05 at concentrations ranging from 22 to 89 µg/m³.

These soil gas results support the conclusion that a soil vapor mitigation system will be required beneath any enclosed structure constructed over the affected area to prevent the migration of volatile petroleum constituents into indoor air at concentrations that could pose a risk to building occupants.

**[6. Remediation Summary]{.underline}**

Following the completion of the Phase II investigation and confirmation that soil contamination in the northeast corner of Parcel 0821-04-72-4102 exceeded NCDEQ residential PSRGs, Harborview Capital Partners LLC retained Sentinel Environmental Consulting LLC to conduct remediation of the identified petroleum contamination. Remediation activities were performed in September 2024 in accordance with a remediation work plan approved by the NCDEQ Inactive Hazardous Sites Branch.

**6.1 Scope of Remediation**

The primary remediation activity consisted of the excavation and off-site disposal of petroleum-impacted soil from the affected area in the northeast corner of Parcel 0821-04-72-4102. Approximately 1,200 cubic yards of soil were excavated from the affected area, with excavation depths reaching approximately 12 feet below grade in the most heavily impacted zone (corresponding to the area surrounding soil borings SB-06 and SB-07). The excavation was conducted using conventional earthmoving equipment under the oversight of Sentinel field personnel, with continuous air monitoring conducted at the excavation perimeter to ensure worker and community safety.

Confirmation soil samples were collected from the excavation sidewalls and base at the completion of excavation activities. The confirmation sampling results demonstrated that residual contamination remains in situ at concentrations below the NCDEQ non-residential PSRGs throughout the excavation area. However, residual contamination remains above the NCDEQ residential PSRGs in certain areas at depths of 10 to 14 feet below grade, particularly along the eastern property boundary where excavation was limited by the proximity of the adjoining property and critical underground utility infrastructure (a 12-inch sanitary sewer main and associated service laterals). Complete removal of all contamination exceeding residential standards was not feasible without risk of damage to the adjacent underground utilities and potential encroachment onto the adjoining property.

All impacted soil removed during the excavation was transported under proper chain-of-custody documentation and disposed of at the Lee County Environmental Landfill, a permitted Subtitle D solid waste management facility located in Sanford, North Carolina. Waste characterization sampling confirmed that the impacted soil met the acceptance criteria for Subtitle D disposal and did not exhibit hazardous waste characteristics under 40 C.F.R. Part 261.

Groundwater encountered during excavation was managed in accordance with an NCDEQ-approved water management plan. Approximately 45,000 gallons of groundwater were pumped from the excavation, treated through granular activated carbon filtration, and discharged under a temporary NPDES general permit.

**6.2 Post-Remediation Monitoring**

Two rounds of post-remediation groundwater monitoring were conducted, on September 15 and October 1, 2024, respectively. Groundwater samples collected from monitoring wells MW-01, MW-02, and MW-03 exhibited decreasing concentrations of dissolved petroleum constituents. All dissolved-phase constituents were detected at concentrations below the applicable North Carolina 2L Groundwater Quality Standards in both monitoring rounds, indicating that the excavation remediation has effectively reduced the dissolved-phase groundwater contamination to below regulatory standards.

**6.3 Remediation Cost**

The total cost of the remediation activities, including excavation, soil disposal, water management, confirmation sampling, and post-remediation monitoring, was approximately \$485,000. This cost was funded by Harborview Capital Partners LLC.

**[7. NCDEQ No Further Action (NFA) Letter --- Summary of Conditions]{.underline}**

On September 30, 2024, the North Carolina Department of Environmental Quality, Inactive Hazardous Sites Branch, issued a No Further Action (\"NFA\") determination letter for Site ID IHSB-24-1203 / Incident No. NONUST-24-0847 (the \"NFA Letter\"). The NFA Letter was addressed to Harborview Capital Partners LLC as the current property owner and responsible party. A complete copy of the NFA Letter is attached as Appendix E to the full Phase I ESA report. The following is a summary of the material terms and conditions of the NFA Letter.

The NFA Letter states that, based on a review of the Phase II investigation data, the remediation completion report, and the post-remediation groundwater monitoring results, NCDEQ has determined that no further remediation action is required at the Subject Property at this time. This determination is expressly conditioned upon compliance with the following requirements:

**Condition 1 --- Soil Vapor Mitigation System.** A soil vapor mitigation system must be installed beneath any enclosed structure constructed over the affected area, which is identified as the approximately 0.38-acre area in the northeast corner of Parcel 0821-04-72-4102, as delineated in the Phase II investigation report and shown on Figure 3 of this report. The NFA Letter specifies that the system shall consist of a passive sub-slab depressurization system with the capability for conversion to an active depressurization system if subsequent monitoring indicates that passive ventilation is insufficient to maintain indoor air quality below applicable screening levels. The system must be designed by a licensed professional engineer registered in the State of North Carolina and must be installed in accordance with NCDEQ Division of Waste Management guidelines for vapor intrusion mitigation. As-built drawings and a system performance verification report must be submitted to NCDEQ within 90 days of the completion of the building foundation in the affected area.

**Condition 2 --- Land Use Restriction (Non-Residential).** The NFA determination is issued on the basis that the affected portion of the Subject Property --- the approximately 0.38-acre area in the northeast corner of Parcel 0821-04-72-4102 --- will be restricted to non-residential use. The NFA Letter states, in relevant part:

> \"Residual soil contamination concentrations in the affected area exceed the NCDEQ Preliminary Soil Remediation Goals for residential land use. Accordingly, this No Further Action determination is contingent upon the restriction of future use of the affected area to non-residential (commercial or industrial) purposes. Any change in land use to residential or other sensitive use on the affected portion of the parcel would require additional investigation and/or remediation to demonstrate that such use is protective of human health and the environment, and a modification to this NFA determination would need to be obtained from NCDEQ prior to such change in use.\"

This non-residential use restriction is the central condition of the NFA Letter and has direct implications for the proposed development of the Subject Property, as discussed further in Sections 8 and 10 of this report.

**Condition 3 --- Soil Management Plan.** Any future excavation, grading, or soil disturbance within the affected area must be conducted in accordance with a NCDEQ-approved soil management plan to ensure proper identification, handling, and disposal of residual contaminated soil. The soil management plan must address procedures for soil screening, stockpile management, dust control, worker health and safety, and disposal of any excavated soil that exceeds applicable waste characterization thresholds. The NFA Letter requires that the soil management plan be submitted to and approved by NCDEQ prior to commencement of any construction activities involving subsurface disturbance within the affected area.

**Condition 4 --- Deed Notice.** The property owner is required to record a notice in the Durham County Registry of Deeds providing notice to future purchasers, lessees, and other parties of the residual contamination present within the affected area and the land use restriction applicable to the affected area. The NFA Letter requires this deed notice to be recorded within 60 days of the date of the NFA Letter --- that is, by November 29, 2024. The deed notice must include a description of the affected area by metes and bounds or by reference to a recorded plat, a description of the nature and extent of residual contamination, and a statement of the non-residential use restriction.

As of the date of this Phase I ESA (October 28, 2024), the consultant was not provided evidence that the required deed notice has been recorded. The 60-day recording deadline of November 29, 2024, had not yet passed as of the assessment date. The client should ensure timely recording of the deed notice to maintain compliance with the NFA conditions.

It is important to note that the NFA Letter does not constitute a \"clean closure\" or a determination that the Subject Property is free of all environmental contamination. The NFA Letter expressly acknowledges that residual petroleum contamination remains in the subsurface within the affected area at concentrations exceeding residential PSRGs. The NFA determination is site-specific and applies only to the conditions known at the time of its issuance. Changes in site conditions, regulatory standards, or land use that are inconsistent with the conditions of the NFA Letter could require reopening the regulatory file and additional investigation or remediation.

**[8. Findings and Identified Environmental Conditions]{.underline}**

Based on the research, investigation, site reconnaissance, and analysis conducted as part of this Phase I Environmental Site Assessment, Sentinel has identified the following environmental conditions at the Subject Property in accordance with the classification framework established by ASTM Standard Practice E1527-21.

**8.1 Recognized Environmental Conditions (RECs)**

**One REC was identified at the Subject Property:**

Residual petroleum contamination, consisting of total petroleum hydrocarbons --- diesel range organics (\"TPH-DRO\") and benzene, is present in soil and soil gas in the northeast corner of Parcel 0821-04-72-4102, in the area of a former 2,000-gallon diesel underground storage tank. The contamination affects an area of approximately 0.38 acres. Although remediation has been conducted and a conditional NFA letter has been issued by NCDEQ, the NFA is premised upon ongoing compliance with specified conditions, and residual contamination remains in place at concentrations exceeding the NCDEQ residential Preliminary Soil Remediation Goals for both TPH-DRO and benzene in soil. Volatile organic compounds in soil gas within the affected area also exceed NCDEQ residential vapor intrusion screening levels.

This condition constitutes a REC as defined in ASTM E1527-21, Section 3.2.84, because the presence of residual petroleum contamination above unrestricted use standards represents \"the presence or likely presence of any hazardous substances or petroleum products in, on, or at a property: (i) due to a release to the environment; (ii) under conditions indicative of a release to the environment; or (iii) under conditions that pose a material threat of a future release to the environment.\"

*Note regarding classification as REC versus CREC:* The consultant considered whether this condition should be classified as a Controlled Recognized Environmental Condition (\"CREC\") rather than a REC. Under ASTM E1527-21, Section 3.2.25, a CREC is defined as \"a recognized environmental condition resulting from a past release of hazardous substances or petroleum products that has been addressed to the satisfaction of the applicable regulatory authority...with hazardous substances or petroleum products allowed to remain in place subject to the implementation of required controls.\" Given that NCDEQ has issued an NFA determination with conditions --- including the soil vapor mitigation requirement, land use restriction, soil management plan, and deed notice --- this condition possesses many characteristics of a CREC. However, as of the date of this assessment, the required deed notice had not yet been recorded in the Durham County Registry of Deeds, and the required soil vapor mitigation system had not yet been designed or installed. Because the NFA conditions have not been fully implemented, the consultant has classified this condition as a REC, representing a conservative and protective approach. Upon full implementation of all NFA conditions --- including recording of the deed notice, installation and verification of the vapor mitigation system, and submittal of the soil management plan --- this condition may be reclassified as a CREC in a future assessment update.

**8.2 Controlled Recognized Environmental Conditions (CRECs)**

No Controlled Recognized Environmental Conditions were identified at the Subject Property as of the date of this assessment. As noted above, the identified REC may be reclassified as a CREC in the future upon full implementation of all NCDEQ NFA conditions.

The conditional NFA land use restriction limiting the affected 0.38-acre area in the northeast corner of Parcel 0821-04-72-4102 to non-residential use may constitute a business environmental risk to the Client and its lender if the proposed development includes residential use of the affected area.
