**[10. Recommendations]{.underline}**

Based on the findings, identified environmental conditions, and conclusions set forth in this Phase I Environmental Site Assessment, Sentinel Environmental Consulting LLC offers the following recommendations to the Client and the Lender.

**Recommendation 1 --- Verify Spatial Relationship of Residential Units to Restricted Area.** The Client and its project architect (Meridian Design Collective PC) should verify whether any proposed residential units in The Piedmont at Brightleaf development will be positioned directly above the approximately 0.38-acre area in the northeast corner of Parcel 0821-04-72-4102 that is subject to the NCDEQ non-residential use restriction under the NFA Letter. This verification should be accomplished by overlaying the proposed building floor plans (including unit layouts for floors 2 through 6) with the environmental delineation map prepared as part of the Phase II investigation (reproduced as Figure 3 in this report). If the overlay confirms that residential units are planned directly above the affected area, the Client should consult with qualified environmental legal counsel regarding the need to either (a) obtain a formal modification to the NFA determination from NCDEQ permitting residential use of the affected area, which would likely require additional environmental investigation, risk assessment, and potentially additional remediation to demonstrate that residential use is protective of human health and the environment under a 30-year residential exposure scenario, or (b) redesign the project to eliminate residential uses above the affected area, such as by repositioning the residential unit layout or converting the affected portion of the upper floors to non-residential uses (e.g., common areas, amenity spaces, or commercial uses). The cost and timeline implications of either approach should be carefully evaluated by the Client, its design team, and its lender.

**Recommendation 2 --- Soil Vapor Mitigation System Design and Installation.** The Client should engage a licensed professional engineer to design the required soil vapor mitigation system for any enclosed space --- including the structured parking garage and any ground-floor retail space --- constructed over the affected area in the northeast corner of Parcel 0821-04-72-4102. The system should be designed as a passive sub-slab depressurization system with conversion capability to active depressurization, as specified in the NFA Letter. Design of the vapor mitigation system should commence during the construction design development phase to ensure that the system is fully integrated into the building foundation and structural plans. As-built drawings and a performance verification report must be submitted to NCDEQ within 90 days of the completion of the building foundation in the affected area, as required by the NFA Letter.

**Recommendation 3 --- Record Deed Notice.** The NFA Letter requires the recording of a deed notice in the Durham County Registry of Deeds within 60 days of September 30, 2024 --- that is, by November 29, 2024. The deed notice must describe the affected area, the nature of the residual contamination, and the non-residential use restriction. The Client should confirm that this deed notice has been or will be timely prepared, reviewed by legal counsel, and recorded. Failure to record the deed notice within the required timeframe could jeopardize the NFA status and may constitute non-compliance with the conditions of the NFA determination. The Client\'s environmental counsel should also review the form and content of the deed notice to ensure that it is consistent with the NFA Letter requirements and does not inadvertently create title encumbrances or restrictions beyond those required by NCDEQ.

**Recommendation 4 --- Soil Management Plan.** A soil management plan should be prepared and submitted to NCDEQ for review and approval prior to commencement of any excavation, grading, or other subsurface disturbance activities within the affected area. The soil management plan should address procedures for visual and olfactory screening of excavated soils, stockpile management, dust suppression, personal protective equipment requirements, worker health and safety protocols, and disposal of any excavated soil that exceeds waste characterization thresholds. All construction personnel working within or adjacent to the affected area should receive training on the potential for encountering contaminated soil and the procedures established in the soil management plan. The soil management plan should be incorporated into the construction specifications and made available to the general contractor (Graystone Construction Group Inc.) and all relevant subcontractors.

**Recommendation 5 --- Ongoing Indoor Air Quality and Soil Gas Monitoring.** The Client should consider voluntarily conducting periodic indoor air quality monitoring or sub-slab soil gas monitoring after construction of any enclosed spaces over the affected area to verify the continued effectiveness of the soil vapor mitigation system. While such monitoring is not expressly required by the NFA Letter, it would provide ongoing documentation that indoor air quality is maintained below applicable screening levels and would serve as an additional safeguard for building occupants. Monitoring should be conducted at a frequency and according to a protocol approved by a qualified environmental professional.

**Recommendation 6 --- Environmental Insurance.** The Client and the Lender (Pinnacle Savings Bank, N.A.) may wish to evaluate the merits of obtaining a pollution legal liability (\"PLL\") insurance policy to address potential environmental liability associated with the residual contamination at the Subject Property. A PLL policy could provide coverage for costs associated with, among other things, obtaining an NFA modification from NCDEQ, conducting additional remediation if required, defending against third-party claims related to the contamination, and responding to unknown environmental conditions that may be discovered during construction. The availability, terms, and cost of PLL coverage should be discussed with a qualified environmental insurance broker.

An environmental indemnity agreement will be required from both the Borrower and the Guarantors (Elena Vasquez-Torres and Reginald K. Section 9: Risk Factors and Mitigants
9.1 Risk Factor: LTC Ratio Exceedance and Zero Cash Equity
Risk. The loan-to-cost ratio of 83.77% exceeds the Bank's maximum permitted LTC of 80% as set forth in both the executed term sheet and the Bank's Commercial Real Estate Lending Policy. The Borrower is contributing zero dollars ($0) in direct cash equity to the Project. The only equity in the capital stack is the previously acquired land, which has an as-is appraised value of $8,900,000 and was acquired for $8,200,000. A portion of the capital used to fund the land acquisition was sourced from Brightleaf Investors Group LLC, an affiliate of the mezzanine lender, Brightleaf Mezzanine Capital LLC. The combined senior loan and mezzanine loan totals $56,700,000, which equals 100% of total project costs, resulting in zero true equity cushion beyond the embedded value in the land.
Impact. The Bank has an outsized exposure relative to total project costs. In a default scenario, the Bank's recovery would depend entirely on the collateral value of the Project and the guarantor resources. The absence of any cash equity contribution means the Borrower has limited "skin in the game" from a cash perspective, which increases moral hazard risk — the risk that the Borrower may be less motivated to resolve problems or fund cost overruns if the Borrower has no cash at risk. The 100% combined leverage ratio means that any decline in project value below total development costs would result in a loss position for one or both lenders, with the senior lender bearing the risk of value declines below the $47,500,000 senior loan balance.
Mitigants. (a) The Bank will require the Borrower to deposit $2,140,000 in cash into a Bank-controlled equity escrow account prior to closing, which will be disbursed ahead of loan advances to fund project costs and bring the effective LTC into compliance with the 80% maximum. (b) The land has an appraised value of $8,900,000, which is $700,000 above the acquisition cost, providing embedded equity. (c) The LTV ratios are well within the Bank's policy limits (65.25% as-completed, 62.34% as-stabilized), indicating adequate value coverage. (d) The combined guarantor net worth of $41,300,000 provides substantial credit support beyond the collateral. (e) The completion and carry guarantees obligate the guarantors to fund cost overruns and cover carrying costs, providing protection against construction budget and timeline risks.
Residual Concern. Even with the equity escrow, the Borrower's total equity contribution would be only $2,140,000 in cash plus $8,200,000 in land (at cost) = $10,340,000 out of $56,700,000 in total project costs = approximately 18.2%. This is relatively thin for a ground-up construction loan, where the Bank's policy guidance generally targets borrower equity contributions of 20% or more. However, the strong LTV position and guarantor support mitigate this concern to an acceptable level.
9.2 Risk Factor: Interest Reserve Adequacy
Risk. As analyzed in Section 6.2, the $4,850,000 interest reserve funded from loan proceeds at closing may be insufficient by approximately $565,000 under current rate assumptions and a reasonable incremental draw assumption. If SOFR increases by 100 basis points, the estimated shortfall would widen to approximately $1,278,000.
Impact. If the interest reserve is depleted before construction completion, the Borrower must fund monthly interest payments from its own resources. Given the Borrower's zero cash equity contribution, the Borrower may lack immediate liquidity to fund interest shortfalls, potentially creating a payment default during the construction period. A payment default during construction could trigger cross-defaults under the mezzanine loan and could jeopardize the construction timeline if the Bank suspends further advances.
Mitigants. (a) The loan documentation will include a mandatory borrower replenishment obligation requiring the Borrower to fund any interest reserve shortfall from its own funds upon demand by the Bank. (b) Interest reserve adequacy will be tested at each draw request, with the Borrower required to replenish the reserve if projected remaining interest costs during the construction period exceed the remaining reserve balance. (c) The guarantors maintain combined liquidity of $9,300,000, which provides a backstop for interest reserve replenishment. (d) The interest reserve analysis assumes a current SOFR of approximately 4.35%. If SOFR rates decline during the construction period, the reserve could prove adequate or even generate a surplus.
Recommendation. The Senior Loan Committee approves the $4,850,000 interest reserve as adequate based on current rate assumptions, with mandatory contractual protections as described above. The Bank should monitor SOFR rate trends closely and communicate proactively with the Borrower regarding any anticipated replenishment obligations.
9.3 Risk Factor: Mezzanine Lender Affiliate Relationship and SPE Concerns
Risk. Brightleaf Investors Group LLC (28% member of the Borrower) shares common control with Brightleaf Mezzanine Capital LLC (mezzanine lender) through Thomas R. Chen. This common control creates a structural conflict and raises the following specific concerns:
First, the mezzanine lender is providing $9,200,000 in subordinated debt to a borrower in which its affiliate holds a significant (28%) equity interest. This interrelationship blurs the distinction between debt and equity in the Borrower's capital structure and may complicate the enforcement of remedies in a default or insolvency scenario.
Second, the affiliate relationship increases substantive consolidation risk. In a bankruptcy proceeding involving the Borrower, a court could potentially substantively consolidate the assets and liabilities of the Borrower with those of Brightleaf Investors Group LLC, Brightleaf Mezzanine Capital LLC, or other entities under common control with Thomas R. Chen. Substantive consolidation would merge the separate estates into a single bankruptcy estate, potentially subordinating the Bank's claims, complicating the Bank's realization upon its collateral, or exposing the collateral to the claims of creditors of the affiliated entities.
Third, the Borrower's intended status as a single-purpose entity requires strict separateness from its members and their affiliates. Standard SPE covenants mandate separate books and records, no commingling of funds, arm's-length transactions, separate corporate formalities, and restrictions on affiliate dealings. The affiliate structure between a Borrower member and the mezzanine lender creates inherent tension with these separateness requirements.
Impact. If SPE covenants are inadequate or are not faithfully observed, the Bank's collateral position could be compromised in a bankruptcy or insolvency proceeding involving the Borrower or any affiliated entity. The risk of substantive consolidation, while relatively uncommon in practice, is heightened in situations where affiliated entities have overlapping ownership, shared management, commingled funds, or inadequate corporate formalities.
Mitigants. The Bank requires the following protective measures as conditions of closing:
(a) Robust SPE Covenants. The loan agreement must include comprehensive SPE covenants requiring the Borrower to: maintain its existence as a separate legal entity; maintain separate books, records, and bank accounts; conduct all transactions with affiliates on arm's-length terms; refrain from commingling its assets or funds with those of any member, affiliate, or other person; observe all limited liability company formalities; hold itself out as an entity separate and distinct from its members and their affiliates; and pay its own liabilities and expenses from its own funds.
(b) Independent Manager. The Borrower's operating agreement must be amended to require the appointment of at least one independent manager (who is not an officer, director, employee, or affiliate of the Borrower, any member, or the mezzanine lender) whose affirmative vote is required for any voluntary filing for bankruptcy, reorganization, or insolvency protection. This provision is the single most important structural safeguard against a bad-faith bankruptcy filing.
(c) Non-Consolidation Opinion. Borrower's counsel (Calloway & Strauss PLLC) must deliver, at closing, a non-consolidation opinion addressed to the Bank, opining that, subject to customary assumptions and qualifications, a court applying applicable North Carolina law would not substantively consolidate the Borrower with any of its members, affiliates, or other related entities. This opinion provides additional assurance (though not a guarantee) that the Borrower's separate existence will be respected in a judicial proceeding.
(d) Intercreditor Provisions. The intercreditor agreement must include express acknowledgments of the affiliate relationship and provisions prohibiting the mezzanine lender from filing or joining in the filing of an involuntary bankruptcy petition against the Borrower.
Market Standard. For securitization-eligible construction loans, industry-standard SPE requirements include independent director or independent manager provisions and non-consolidation opinions from borrower's counsel. While this loan is not currently intended for securitization, implementing these protections is prudent given the heightened affiliate risk. The analytical framework for non-consolidation analysis draws on Delaware LLC law principles (even though the Borrower is a North Carolina LLC), as the Delaware case law provides the most developed body of precedent on substantive consolidation in the context of structured finance transactions.
9.4 Risk Factor: Conflicting Membership Interest Pledges
Risk. Both the senior construction loan and the mezzanine loan are secured by a pledge of 100% of the membership interests in the Borrower. As a matter of law and commercial practice, only one lender can hold a first-priority security interest in the same collateral. As currently documented, the pledges are mutually exclusive as first-priority interests, creating an ambiguity that could result in litigation or contested priority in a default scenario.
Impact. If the conflicting pledges are not resolved, the Bank may not have the collateral position described in the term sheet. In a default, the mezzanine lender could assert a competing first-priority claim to the membership interests, and the resulting dispute could delay or prevent the Bank's exercise of remedies, including foreclosure on the membership interests or exercise of control over the Borrower.
Mitigants. Execution of the intercreditor agreement (currently negotiated but not yet executed) must be a condition precedent to closing. The intercreditor agreement must provide: (i) the senior lender (Pinnacle Savings Bank, N.A.) holds a first-priority security interest in both the real property collateral and the membership interests; (ii) the mezzanine lender (Brightleaf Mezzanine Capital LLC) holds a subordinated second-priority security interest in the membership interests; (iii) the mezzanine lender is subject to a 90-day standstill period before exercising any remedies; (iv) the mezzanine lender has cure rights and a purchase option (right to acquire the senior loan at par plus accrued); and (v) the mezzanine lender may not modify the terms of the mezzanine loan without the Bank's prior written consent.
Alternative. If the intercreditor agreement cannot be finalized on terms satisfactory to the Bank, the Bank could forego the membership interest pledge and rely solely on its real property collateral (first-priority deed of trust, assignment of rents and leases, security interest in personal property). The LTV ratios support the real property collateral alone. However, the membership interest pledge provides an additional layer of protection and operational control that the Bank considers valuable, particularly in a construction loan context where the Bank needs the ability to step in and control the development entity if the Borrower defaults.
Recommendation. The Bank requires execution of the intercreditor agreement as a hard closing condition. The loan may not close without a fully executed and delivered intercreditor agreement in form and substance satisfactory to the Bank and its counsel.
9.5 Risk Factor: Environmental Use Restriction / Residential Conflict
Risk. The NFA letter issued by NCDEQ on September 30, 2024 restricts the approximately 0.38-acre area in the northeast corner of Parcel 0821-04-72-4102 to non-residential use. However, the current project plans position 14 residential units in the building structure directly above this area at the podium level and upper floors.
Impact. If this conflict is not resolved, those 14 units may not receive residential certificates of occupancy from the City of Durham, which would reduce the Project's rental income and adversely affect the Bank's underwriting assumptions. The estimated annual revenue impact of losing 14 residential units is approximately $377,160 (14 units × $2,245 average monthly rent × 12 months). This would reduce the stabilized NOI to approximately $4,499,640 ($4,876,800 − $377,160), and the recalculated DSCR would be approximately $4,499,640 ÷ $3,728,750 = 1.21x, which is below the Bank's minimum of 1.25x. Additionally, the as-completed and as-stabilized appraised values may be overstated if they assume occupancy and income from the affected 14 units without accounting for the use restriction.
Mitigants. The Bank requires the Borrower, as a condition of closing (or, at the Bank's discretion, as a condition precedent to advances for construction above the podium level in the affected area), to achieve one of the following resolutions: (a) obtain a modification to the NFA letter from NCDEQ permitting residential use of the area, contingent on installation and ongoing maintenance of the soil vapor mitigation system; (b) redesign the 14 affected units as commercial or retail space and provide updated financial projections; or (c) provide written confirmation from NCDEQ that residential use is permitted in the floors above the grade-level restricted area, provided that appropriate engineering controls (including the vapor mitigation system) are in place and operational.
Recommendation. The Bank flags this issue for review by outside counsel and environmental consultants. The resolution approach should be documented as a specific covenant in the loan documentation, and the Bank should retain discretion to withhold advances for construction in the affected area until the issue is resolved to the Bank's satisfaction.
9.6 Risk Factor: Construction Timeline and Market Risk
Risk. The 30-month construction period targets projected substantial completion on August 31, 2027. The construction maturity date under the loan is August 28, 2027 — only three days before the projected substantial completion date. Any construction delay, even a minor one, could push substantial completion past the construction maturity date, triggering a maturity default under the loan.
Mitigants. The mini-perm period provides an additional 12 months following the construction maturity date (extending to August 28, 2028), plus the 6-month extension option (to February 28, 2029). These periods provide a substantial buffer for the Borrower to complete construction, achieve stabilization, and arrange permanent take-out financing. The GMP contract with Graystone Construction Group Inc. provides cost certainty (subject to approved change orders), and the contingency of $1,440,000 provides approximately 4.1% cushion on hard construction costs. The completion guaranty from both guarantors provides the Bank with recourse against the guarantors' personal assets in the event construction is not completed.
Market Risk. The Durham multifamily market is currently strong, but the 30-month construction horizon introduces inherent uncertainty regarding supply, demand, and rental rate trends. The 5% vacancy assumption is adequate based on historical trends, and the Bank considers the risk of a significant market downturn during the construction period to be moderate but not negligible. The Bank will monitor market conditions throughout the construction period and may require updated market studies as a condition of the extension option.
9.7 Risk Factor: Title — Unsatisfied Prior Deed of Trust
Risk. The title commitment issued by Aldersgate Title & Escrow Inc. (Commitment No. NC-2024-88712, dated December 5, 2024, escrow officer Patricia Langley) identifies an unsatisfied deed of trust recorded in favor of Triangle Commercial Bank, dated 2018, encumbering the Property and securing indebtedness of $3,400,000. Borrower's counsel (Jonathan F. Ngo, Calloway & Strauss PLLC) represents that this deed of trust will be satisfied at closing from the proceeds of the senior construction loan or from borrower funds.
Impact. If the prior deed of trust is not satisfied and released at closing, the Bank would not hold a first-priority lien on the Property as required under the loan terms.
Mitigant. Closing is conditioned on receipt of a satisfactory title insurance policy from Aldersgate Title & Escrow Inc. insuring the first-priority lien of the Bank's deed of trust, free and clear of the prior Triangle Commercial Bank deed of trust. The Bank requires delivery of a payoff letter from Triangle Commercial Bank and simultaneous recording of the satisfaction or release of the prior deed of trust with the recording of the Bank's deed of trust. The title insurance policy must be issued without any exception for the prior deed of trust.
9.8 Additional Risk Considerations
Brightleaf Historic District Association CC&Rs. The Property is located within the Brightleaf Historic District, which is subject to Covenants, Conditions, and Restrictions recorded in Book 6984, Page 1155 of the Durham County Register of Deeds. The CC&Rs include architectural review and design standards that may affect the design and construction of the Project. The Bank requires, as a condition of closing, evidence that the Brightleaf Historic District Association has reviewed and approved the Project plans, or that the CC&Rs do not apply to the Project or have been waived with respect to the Project.
Interest Rate Risk. The loan bears a floating interest rate based on Daily Simple SOFR, which exposes both the Bank and the Borrower to interest rate volatility. As demonstrated in the stress test analysis (Section 6.1), a 200-basis-point increase in SOFR would push the projected stabilized DSCR to 1.04x, well below the Bank's minimum. The Bank should consider requiring the Borrower to obtain an interest rate cap agreement for the mini-perm period and any extension period. The loan documentation must include SOFR benchmark replacement provisions consistent with the Alternative Reference Rates Committee ("ARRC") recommended fallback language.
Guarantor Concentration in Illiquid Assets. Both guarantors have personal net worth heavily concentrated in real estate holdings. Ms. Vasquez-Torres's real estate holdings constitute approximately 65% of her total net worth, and Mr. Osei's constitute approximately 59%. A decline in real estate values could erode guarantor net worth and impair their ability to perform under the guarantees.
General Contractor Risk. Graystone Construction Group Inc.'s GMP contract provides cost certainty for hard construction costs. The Bank should verify the financial strength and payment and performance bonding capacity of the contractor prior to closing. Evidence of the contractor's financial statements and bonding capacity should be included in the closing deliverables.

Based on the land residual analysis performed in the full appraisal report, a mixed-use residential and retail development of the type and scale proposed for the subject was determined to produce the highest land residual value and is therefore concluded to represent the highest and best use of the land as if vacant.

**[As Proposed (Improved)]{.underline}**

The highest and best use of the property as proposed --- that is, assuming construction of the 212-unit mixed-use residential and retail development as described in Section 3 --- satisfies all four tests. The proposed development is legally permissible under MU-D zoning without the need for variances or special permits. It is physically possible given the site\'s dimensions, topography, and infrastructure availability. It is financially feasible based on the income projections and cost analysis set forth in this report, which indicate that the prospective stabilized net operating income will support a market value in excess of the total development cost. Finally, the proposed development is maximally productive relative to alternative development programs analyzed by the appraiser, as it generates the highest return on cost among the programs considered.

**[Conclusion]{.underline}**

The proposed development of The Piedmont at Brightleaf --- a 212-unit Class A mixed-use residential and retail project --- represents the highest and best use of the subject property, both as if vacant and as proposed.

**[Section 6 --- Valuation Methodology and Conclusions]{.underline}**

**[Section 6.1 --- As-Is Land Valuation]{.underline}**

**Approach:** The as-is market value of the subject land was estimated using the sales comparison approach, which is the most reliable and widely accepted methodology for valuing vacant land in an active market with sufficient comparable data. The subject is valued in its current condition as of the effective date: vacant, cleared, and rough-graded, with environmental remediation completed and all municipal utilities available.

**Comparable Land Sales:** The appraiser identified and analyzed four recent sales of comparable development land in the downtown Durham and adjacent urban submarkets. Each comparable was adjusted for differences in location, size, shape, access, utilities, topography, and market conditions (time of sale). The comparable sales and adjustments are summarized below:

**Sale 1:** A 2.81-acre parcel located on West Chapel Hill Street, Durham, sold in July 2024 for \$7,447,000, or \$2,650,000 per acre. The parcel is zoned for mixed-use development and is located approximately 0.5 miles west of the subject. After adjustment for the subject\'s superior street frontage and slightly less favorable vehicular access from a secondary roadway, the adjusted rate is \$2,510,000 per acre.

**Sale 2:** A 1.95-acre parcel located on Morris Street, Durham, sold in April 2024 for \$5,460,000, or \$2,800,000 per acre. The parcel is smaller than the subject and has a more regular shape, which typically commands a premium on a per-acre basis for efficient development. After adjustment for the subject\'s larger size and irregular configuration, the adjusted rate is \$2,620,000 per acre.

**Sale 3:** A 4.12-acre parcel located on Mangum Street, Durham, sold in January 2024 for \$9,888,000, or \$2,400,000 per acre. The parcel is located in a transitional area approximately 0.7 miles north of the downtown core and was adjusted upward for the subject\'s superior Brightleaf district location and proximity to established amenities. The adjusted rate is \$2,550,000 per acre.

**Sale 4:** A 3.05-acre assemblage of two parcels located on Corporation Street, Durham, sold in September 2023 for \$7,168,000, or \$2,350,000 per acre. The sale occurred approximately 14 months prior to the effective date and was adjusted upward for market conditions (positive price trend in downtown Durham land values) and for the subject\'s superior frontage and access. The adjusted rate is \$2,480,000 per acre.

**Indicated Value Range:** The adjusted comparable sales indicate a range of \$2,480,000 to \$2,620,000 per acre for the subject land.

**Selected Rate:** After reconciliation of the comparable data, placing greatest weight on Sales 1 and 3 as most similar in size and location to the subject, the appraiser selected a rate of approximately \$2,565,000 per acre.

**As-Is Land Value:** 3.47 acres × \$2,565,000 per acre = \$8,900,550, rounded to **\$8,900,000**.

**Reconciliation:** The concluded as-is land value of \$8,900,000 is consistent with the land acquisition cost of \$8,200,000, which was the price paid by Harborview Capital Partners LLC in early 2024 prior to the demolition of the existing warehouse structures and the completion of environmental remediation. The demolition and remediation activities, which cost approximately \$680,000, have contributed to the current enhanced value of the land in its cleared and development-ready condition.

**[Section 6.2 --- As-Completed Valuation]{.underline}**

**Approaches Used:** The as-completed market value of the subject property was estimated using the income capitalization approach as the primary valuation methodology, supported by the sales comparison approach as a secondary check on reasonableness.

**Income Capitalization Approach**

The \"as-completed\" value reflects the market value of the proposed development upon completion of construction but prior to the achievement of stabilized occupancy. This valuation scenario recognizes that, at the point of construction completion, the property will not yet have reached its projected stabilized occupancy of 95% and the owner will incur costs and experience income loss during the lease-up period. Accordingly, the as-completed value is derived by deducting from the as-stabilized value the estimated costs and economic impact of the lease-up period.

The prospective stabilized net operating income (\"NOI\") of the subject, as detailed in Section 7 below, is \$4,876,800 per annum. Applied at the selected capitalization rate of 6.40%, the indicated as-stabilized value is \$76,200,000 (see Section 6.3 below).

**Lease-Up Deductions from As-Stabilized Value:**

The appraiser estimated the following deductions to account for the lease-up period between construction completion and stabilization:

> • **Estimated lease-up period:** 9 months (midpoint of the 8- to 10-month range projected in Section 4), commencing upon receipt of the certificate of occupancy.
>
> • **Lost rental income during lease-up:** Assuming a linear absorption from 0% to 95% occupancy over the 9-month period, the effective average occupancy during lease-up is approximately 47.5%. The resulting lost rental income relative to stabilized occupancy (95%) is estimated at approximately \$2,450,000.
>
> • **Lease-up costs:** Additional marketing expenditures, concessions to early tenants (estimated at an average of one month\'s free rent per unit), and supplemental on-site leasing staff are estimated to total approximately \$680,000.
>
> • **Total lease-up adjustment:** Approximately \$3,130,000.
>
> • **Discount for lease-up risk and timing:** An additional deduction of approximately \$270,000 is applied to account for the risk and present-value discount associated with the timing uncertainty of the lease-up period.
>
> • **Total deduction from as-stabilized value:** \$3,130,000 + \$270,000 = \$3,400,000.

**As-Completed Value via Income Approach:** \$76,200,000 − \$3,400,000 = **\$72,800,000**.

**Sales Comparison Approach (Supportive)**

As a supportive check on the income capitalization approach, the appraiser analyzed three comparable sales of recently constructed mixed-use multifamily properties in the Research Triangle area. The sales indicated a price range of \$330,000 to \$360,000 per residential unit, after adjustment for the retail component. Applied to the subject\'s 212 residential units, the midpoint of approximately \$343,000 per unit indicates a value of approximately \$72,700,000, which is highly supportive of the income approach conclusion.

**Concluded As-Completed Market Value: \$72,800,000**

**[Section 6.3 --- As-Stabilized Valuation]{.underline}**

**Approach:** The as-stabilized market value was estimated using the income capitalization approach, specifically the direct capitalization method.

**Stabilization Assumption:** Stabilized occupancy is defined as 95% across all residential units and retail bays, consistent with the observed stabilized occupancy levels at the comparable properties in the downtown Durham submarket.

**Projected Stabilization Date:** The appraiser projects that the subject will achieve stabilized occupancy approximately nine months following projected substantial completion, or approximately May 2028.

**Capitalization Rate Analysis:** The overall capitalization rate was derived from an analysis of five comparable property sales in the Raleigh-Durham metropolitan market, all involving Class A multifamily or mixed-use residential properties with recent construction dates. The observed capitalization rates for these transactions ranged from 5.75% to 7.10%, with a mean of approximately 6.35% and a median of approximately 6.40%. The variance in observed rates reflects differences in property quality, location, tenant profile, and the proportion of retail versus residential income.

**Selected Capitalization Rate: 6.40%.** The selected rate is positioned at the median of the comparable range and reflects the subject\'s status as a new-construction, Class A property in a prime downtown location with strong demand fundamentals. The rate also accounts for the current interest rate environment, which has stabilized following the tightening cycle of 2022-2023, with the 10-year U.S. Treasury yield trading at approximately 4.40% as of the effective date.

**Stabilized Net Operating Income:** \$4,876,800 per annum (as detailed in Section 7 below).

**As-Stabilized Value Calculation:**

\$4,876,800 ÷ 0.0640 = **\$76,200,000**

**Cross-Check:** The indicated as-stabilized value of \$76,200,000 implies a price per residential unit of approximately \$359,434 (\$76,200,000 ÷ 212 units). This metric falls within the range of \$340,000 to \$380,000 per unit observed for Class A new-construction multifamily properties in the downtown Durham submarket, confirming the reasonableness of the valuation conclusion. On a gross building area basis, the indicated value equates to approximately \$265.04 per square foot (\$76,200,000 ÷ 287,500 square feet), which is consistent with comparable market data.

**[Section 8 --- Environmental Considerations]{.underline}**

The appraiser reviewed the Phase I Environmental Site Assessment (\"Phase I ESA\") prepared by Sentinel Environmental Consulting LLC, dated October 28, 2024. The Phase I ESA was prepared by the firm\'s lead environmental consultant, Dr. James Whitfield, P.E., in general conformance with ASTM Standard Practice E 1527-21 for Environmental Site Assessments. The Phase I ESA encompassed both parcels comprising the subject property.

The Phase I ESA identified one Recognized Environmental Condition (\"REC\") affecting the subject property: residual petroleum contamination associated with a former underground storage tank (\"UST\") located on the northeast corner of Parcel 0821-04-72-4102 (615 Foster Street). Historical records indicate that the UST was originally installed in the 1950s in connection with the former tobacco warehouse operations and was used for the storage of heating oil. The UST had not been in active use since approximately 1988.

A Phase II Environmental Site Assessment (\"Phase II ESA\") was subsequently conducted in August 2024, also by Sentinel Environmental Consulting LLC. The Phase II ESA included the advancement of soil borings and the collection and laboratory analysis of soil and groundwater samples from the area surrounding the former UST location. The results of the Phase II ESA revealed petroleum hydrocarbon contamination levels in soil that exceeded the North Carolina Department of Environmental Quality (\"NCDEQ\") Inactive Hazardous Sites Branch (\"IHSB\") residential soil screening levels for certain constituents, including benzene, toluene, ethylbenzene, and xylenes (\"BTEX\"). However, the detected concentrations were below the applicable NCDEQ non-residential (commercial/industrial) soil screening levels.

Environmental remediation of the affected area was completed in September 2024. Remediation activities included the removal and proper disposal of the former UST, excavation and off-site disposal of approximately 320 cubic yards of petroleum-impacted soil, and post-remediation confirmation sampling. The remediation was performed under the oversight of NCDEQ and in accordance with an approved remediation work plan.

Following completion of the remediation, NCDEQ issued a No Further Action (\"NFA\") letter dated September 30, 2024, for the affected area. The NFA letter confirms that no further investigation or remediation is required, subject to the following conditions:

> \(i\) A soil vapor mitigation system must be installed and maintained in the structured parking garage and any enclosed occupied space constructed above the affected area, in accordance with specifications approved by NCDEQ; and
>
> \(ii\) Future use of the affected portion of Parcel 0821-04-72-4102 --- specifically, an area encompassing approximately 0.38 acres in the northeast corner of the parcel --- is restricted to non-residential purposes. This land use restriction is memorialized in a Declaration of Land Use Restrictions recorded at the Durham County Register of Deeds.

The appraiser notes that the soil vapor mitigation system required by the NFA letter has been incorporated into the construction plans and specifications prepared by Meridian Design Collective PC and is included within the GMP contract with Graystone Construction Group Inc. The cost of the vapor mitigation system is reflected in the hard construction cost budget.

The NFA letter restricts future use of the northeast corner of Parcel 0821-04-72-4102 (approximately 0.38 acres) to non-residential use. The appraiser notes this restriction for the record. The project plans, as reviewed by the appraiser and as described by the developer, include residential units on the upper floors of the building positioned above this area of the site. The appraiser\'s valuation assumes that the borrower will comply with all applicable environmental laws, regulations, and use restrictions, and that any required modifications, variances, or additional remediation necessary to permit the planned use will be obtained by the borrower at the borrower\'s cost. The appraiser expresses no opinion as to the legal permissibility of the planned residential use of the area above the environmentally restricted portion of the site. The appraiser has not adjusted the valuation conclusions to account for any potential impact of the NFA use restriction on the residential unit mix or leasability of units positioned above the restricted area.

The appraiser is not an environmental consultant and does not render opinions regarding environmental conditions, remediation adequacy, or compliance with environmental regulations. The reader is directed to the Phase I and Phase II ESA reports prepared by Sentinel Environmental Consulting LLC for a complete discussion of environmental matters.

**[SECTION 1: ORGANIZATIONAL CHART --- HARBORVIEW CAPITAL PARTNERS LLC]{.underline}**

**[1.1 Borrower Entity Overview]{.underline}**

**Harborview Capital Partners LLC** is a limited liability company organized under the laws of the State of North Carolina. The Borrower was formed on **March 14, 2019**, and is registered with the North Carolina Secretary of State under File No. **1923847**. The Borrower\'s principal office is located at **400 West Main Street, Suite 310, Durham, NC 27701**.

The Borrower was formed as a single-purpose entity for the acquisition, development, construction, ownership, and operation of the real property located at 601 and 615 Foster Street, Durham, Durham County, North Carolina 27701 (Parcel IDs: 0821-04-72-3341 and 0821-04-72-4102), commonly known as \"The Piedmont at Brightleaf\" (the \"Project\"). The current net worth of the Borrower entity is approximately **\$14,200,000** based on the book value of its assets and liabilities as of the most recent reporting period.

While the Borrower was formed as a single-purpose entity and operates exclusively in connection with the Project, the Amended and Restated Operating Agreement of the Borrower (as excerpted in Section 2 below) does not currently include provisions for an independent director or independent manager, nor does it contain separateness covenants customarily associated with single-purpose entity structures in commercial real estate finance transactions. Additionally, as detailed in Section 1.2 below, Brightleaf Investors Group LLC, which holds a 28% membership interest in the Borrower, is an affiliate of Brightleaf Mezzanine Capital LLC, the mezzanine lender to the Project, and both entities are under the common control of Thomas R. Chen. This structural relationship warrants review in the context of SPE separateness analysis.

**[1.2 Member Structure (Ownership Chart)]{.underline}**

The following sets forth the ownership structure of Harborview Capital Partners LLC as of the date hereof, presented in two tiers reflecting direct membership interests in the Borrower and the control structure of the entity members.

**Tier 1 --- Members of Harborview Capital Partners LLC**

  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Member**                       **Type**                           **Membership Interest**   **Role**
  -------------------------------- ---------------------------------- ------------------------- -----------------
  Elena Vasquez-Torres             Individual                         62%                       Managing Member

  Brightleaf Investors Group LLC   NC LLC (NC SOS File No. 2045612)   28%                       Member

  Reginald K. Osei                 Individual                         10%                       Member
  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

**Tier 2 --- Control of Brightleaf Investors Group LLC**

Brightleaf Investors Group LLC is a North Carolina limited liability company with its principal office in Durham, North Carolina. The Managing Member of Brightleaf Investors Group LLC is **Thomas R. Chen**. The other members of Brightleaf Investors Group LLC consist of a group of local high-net-worth investors whose identities are available upon request under separate confidentiality agreement.

**Tier 2 --- Affiliate Relationship (Critical Notation)**

**Brightleaf Mezzanine Capital LLC** (NC LLC, NC SOS File No. **2103988**) is an affiliate of Brightleaf Investors Group LLC. Both entities are under the **common control of Thomas R. Chen**, who serves as the Managing Member of both Brightleaf Investors Group LLC and Brightleaf Mezzanine Capital LLC.

Brightleaf Mezzanine Capital LLC is providing a **\$9,200,000 mezzanine loan** to the Borrower at a fixed rate of **12.50% per annum**, secured by a **pledge of 100% of the membership interests** in the Borrower. The mezzanine loan matures coterminous with the senior construction loan from Pinnacle Savings Bank, N.A. The Borrower\'s capital structure, accordingly, includes both an equity member (Brightleaf Investors Group LLC, 28%) and a mezzanine lender (Brightleaf Mezzanine Capital LLC), each under the common control of the same individual.

*Note: The mezzanine loan from Brightleaf Mezzanine Capital LLC is secured by a pledge of 100% of the membership interests in the Borrower. An intercreditor agreement between Pinnacle Savings Bank, N.A. and Brightleaf Mezzanine Capital LLC has been negotiated but is not yet executed as of the date hereof.*

**Notation on Guarantors**

The following individuals have agreed to serve as personal guarantors in connection with the senior construction loan from Pinnacle Savings Bank, N.A.:

**Elena Vasquez-Torres** (62% Member / Managing Member) --- Personal guarantor. Approximate net worth: **\$29.8 million** (liquid assets: \$6.1 million; real estate holdings: \$19.4 million; other assets: \$4.3 million). Ms. Vasquez-Torres has 22 years of commercial real estate development experience and is a resident of Durham, North Carolina.

**Reginald K. Osei** (10% Member) --- Personal guarantor. Approximate net worth: **\$11.5 million** (liquid assets: \$3.2 million; real estate holdings: \$6.8 million; other assets: \$1.5 million). Mr. Osei has 15 years of experience in real estate finance and development and is a resident of Chapel Hill, North Carolina.

Combined guarantor net worth: approximately **\$41.3 million**. Combined guarantor liquidity: **\$9,300,000** (\$6.1M + \$3.2M).

**[1.3 Capital Contributions and Equity Summary]{.underline}**

**Land Contribution.** The real property comprising the Project site (Parcel IDs: 0821-04-72-3341 and 0821-04-72-4102) was contributed to Harborview Capital Partners LLC by **Elena Vasquez-Torres** at a cost basis of **\$8,200,000**. The land was originally acquired by Ms. Vasquez-Torres in a transaction funded from her personal resources and was subsequently contributed to the Borrower upon formation of the project entity. The contribution was reflected on the Borrower\'s books at the **\$8,200,000** acquisition cost basis. For reference, the as-is appraised value of the land per the appraisal by Ridgeline Appraisal Services Inc. dated November 15, 2024 (Appraiser: Linda M. Haverford, MAI) is **\$8,900,000**, which exceeds the acquisition cost basis by \$700,000.

**Member Capital Calls.** The members have funded the following capital contributions to date:

  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Member**                        **Capital Contribution**                        **Source**
  --------------------------------- ----------------------------------------------- --------------------------------
  Elena Vasquez-Torres              \$8,200,000 (land contribution at cost basis)   Personal acquisition of land

  Brightleaf Investors Group LLC    \$0 cash to date                                Future capital calls as needed

  Reginald K. Osei                  \$0 cash to date                                Future capital calls as needed

  **Total member equity to date**   **\$8,200,000**                                 
  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

**Additional Funding Sources.** The total project cost for The Piedmont at Brightleaf is **\$56,700,000**. Beyond the member equity reflected above, the Project is funded as follows:

> • Senior construction loan (Pinnacle Savings Bank, N.A.): **\$47,500,000**
>
> • Mezzanine loan (Brightleaf Mezzanine Capital LLC): **\$9,200,000**
>
> • Additional borrower cash equity: **\$0**
>
> • **Total: \$47,500,000 + \$9,200,000 + \$0 = \$56,700,000**

The foregoing sources and uses summary reflects that there is no additional cash equity contribution from any member beyond the land contribution by Ms. Vasquez-Torres. The entire non-debt funding of the Project consists of the \$8,200,000 land contribution. Brightleaf Investors Group LLC, the 28% member affiliated with the mezzanine lender, has contributed no cash equity to date; its membership interest was issued in consideration of its commitment to arrange third-party mezzanine financing for the Project, as set forth in the Operating Agreement (see Section 2.3 below). The mezzanine loan of \$9,200,000 from Brightleaf Mezzanine Capital LLC, an affiliate of Brightleaf Investors Group LLC, fills the gap between the senior loan proceeds and the total project cost. No independent cash equity beyond the land contribution exists in the capital stack.

**[SECTION 2: EXCERPTS FROM OPERATING AGREEMENT OF HARBORVIEW CAPITAL PARTNERS LLC]{.underline}**

**[2.1 Preamble and Identification]{.underline}**

The following are selected excerpts from the Amended and Restated Operating Agreement of Harborview Capital Partners LLC, dated as of March 14, 2019, as amended through December 1, 2024 (the \"Operating Agreement\"). These excerpts are provided for informational purposes only in connection with the senior construction loan from Pinnacle Savings Bank, N.A. (Loan No. CRE-2025-0342) and do not constitute the complete Operating Agreement. The full Operating Agreement has been provided to Lender\'s counsel, Ashford, Cromdale Consulting & Laine LLP, under separate cover. In the event of any conflict between these excerpts and the full Operating Agreement, the full Operating Agreement shall control.

**[2.2 Excerpt --- Article III: Management and Authority (Section 3.1 --- Managing Member)]{.underline}**

The following is excerpted from Article III, Section 3.1 of the Operating Agreement:

> *Section 3.1 --- Managing Member.* **Elena Vasquez-Torres** shall serve as the sole Managing Member of the Company. The Managing Member shall have the exclusive authority to manage the day-to-day operations and affairs of the Company, including without limitation: (a) entering into contracts on behalf of the Company in the ordinary course of business; (b) hiring and terminating employees, contractors, and consultants; (c) making capital expenditure decisions with respect to the Project in amounts not exceeding Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$500,000) individually (any single expenditure in excess of \$500,000 shall require the prior approval of Members holding a majority in interest of the outstanding membership interests); (d) executing loan documents, promissory notes, deeds of trust, and related instruments on behalf of the Company; and (e) managing and overseeing the construction and development of the Project, including selection of architects, general contractors, and subcontractors.
>
> *Section 3.2 --- Major Decisions.* Notwithstanding the foregoing, the following actions shall require the prior written approval of Members holding at least seventy-five percent (75%) of the outstanding membership interests: (a) any sale, transfer, or encumbrance of all or substantially all of the Company\'s assets; (b) any financing or refinancing of the Property in a principal amount in excess of One Million Dollars (\$1,000,000); (c) the admission of any new Member to the Company; (d) any amendment to this Operating Agreement; and (e) any voluntary dissolution of the Company or the filing of any petition for relief under any federal or state bankruptcy or insolvency law.

The approval threshold of 75% means that Elena Vasquez-Torres (62%) cannot unilaterally approve any major decision. She would require the concurrence of at least one additional member. Combined with Brightleaf Investors Group LLC (28%), the two members hold 90%, which exceeds the 75% threshold. Combined with Reginald K. Osei (10%), Ms. Vasquez-Torres and Mr. Osei hold 72%, which falls below the 75% threshold. Consequently, Brightleaf Investors Group LLC holds an effective veto right over major decisions, as no combination of the other two members alone can reach the required supermajority.

The Operating Agreement, as currently in effect, does not contain any provision requiring the appointment of an independent director or independent manager for the Company. There are no separateness covenants requiring the Company to maintain its own books, records, and bank accounts separate from those of its members or their affiliates, no prohibition on commingling of funds with affiliates, and no requirement that the Company obtain a non-consolidation opinion. These provisions are customarily required by institutional lenders in single-purpose entity structures.

**[2.3 Excerpt --- Article V: Capital Contributions (Section 5.1 --- Initial Capital Contributions; Section 5.3 --- Additional Capital Calls)]{.underline}**

The following is excerpted from Article V, Sections 5.1 and 5.3 of the Operating Agreement:

> *Section 5.1 --- Initial Capital Contributions.* Each Member shall make the following initial capital contributions to the Company:
>
> \(a\) **Elena Vasquez-Torres** shall contribute that certain real property located at 601 and 615 Foster Street, Durham, Durham County, North Carolina 27701 (Parcel IDs: 0821-04-72-3341 and 0821-04-72-4102), together with all improvements, easements, and appurtenances thereto, valued at Eight Million Two Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$8,200,000) (acquisition cost basis), in exchange for a sixty-two percent (62%) membership interest in the Company.
>
> \(b\) **Brightleaf Investors Group LLC** shall make an initial capital contribution of Zero Dollars (\$0) at the time of formation. Brightleaf Investors Group LLC shall receive a twenty-eight percent (28%) membership interest in the Company in consideration of its commitment to arrange third-party mezzanine financing for the Project and to contribute future capital as and when called by the Managing Member in accordance with Section 5.3 of this Agreement.
>
> \(c\) **Reginald K. Osei** shall make an initial capital contribution of Zero Dollars (\$0) at the time of formation. Reginald K. Osei shall receive a ten percent (10%) membership interest in the Company in consideration of development management services to be provided to the Company in connection with the Project and his commitment to contribute future capital as and when called by the Managing Member in accordance with Section 5.3 of this Agreement.
>
> *Section 5.3 --- Additional Capital Calls.* The Managing Member may, from time to time, issue capital calls to all Members pro rata in proportion to their respective membership interests, upon not less than thirty (30) days\' prior written notice. Capital calls shall be at the sole discretion of the Managing Member for purposes of funding Project costs not covered by loan proceeds or other available funds. Any Member who fails to fund a capital call within the applicable notice period shall be subject to dilution of such Member\'s membership interest on a two-to-one (2:1) penalty basis, as calculated in accordance with Schedule B attached hereto.

As reflected above, Brightleaf Investors Group LLC received its 28% membership interest not in exchange for a cash capital contribution but in consideration of its commitment to arrange third-party mezzanine financing for the Project. That mezzanine financing was arranged through Brightleaf Mezzanine Capital LLC, an entity under the common control of Thomas R. Chen, who also serves as Managing Member of Brightleaf Investors Group LLC. The Borrower\'s cash equity position is therefore entirely dependent on the land contribution made by Elena Vasquez-Torres.

**[2.4 Excerpt --- Article VI: Distributions (Section 6.1 --- Distribution Waterfall)]{.underline}**

The following is excerpted from Article VI, Section 6.1 of the Operating Agreement:

> *Section 6.1 --- Distribution Waterfall.* Distributable Cash (as defined in Section 1.1 of this Agreement, being the net cash from operations of the Company or net proceeds from a Capital Event, in each case after payment of all Company obligations, including without limitation debt service on all loans (including the senior construction loan, any mezzanine or subordinate financing, and any other indebtedness of the Company), required reserves, and operating expenses) shall be distributed to the Members in the following order of priority:
>
> \(a\) **First**, to all Members pro rata in proportion to their respective membership interests, until each Member has received a cumulative return equal to a nine percent (9.0%) per annum preferred return on such Member\'s unreturned capital contribution (as calculated on a non-compounded basis from the date of such contribution);
>
> \(b\) **Second**, to all Members pro rata in proportion to their respective membership interests, until each Member has received a return of one hundred percent (100%) of such Member\'s unreturned capital contribution; and
>
> \(c\) **Third**, the balance, if any, shall be distributed seventy percent (70%) to Elena Vasquez-Torres (as the Managing Member), twenty percent (20%) to Brightleaf Investors Group LLC, and ten percent (10%) to Reginald K. Osei (the \"Promote Split\").

The distribution waterfall expressly provides that debt service on \"all loans,\" including any mezzanine or subordinate financing, constitutes a Company obligation that must be satisfied before any distributions are made to the Members. This structure places the mezzanine loan from Brightleaf Mezzanine Capital LLC --- an affiliate of the 28% member, Brightleaf Investors Group LLC --- at a priority ahead of member distributions, further intertwining the financial relationship between the Borrower, its equity members, and the mezzanine lender.

**[2.5 Excerpt --- Article IX: Transfer Restrictions (Section 9.1 --- Restrictions on Transfer)]{.underline}**

The following is excerpted from Article IX, Section 9.1 of the Operating Agreement:

> *Section 9.1 --- Restrictions on Transfer.* No Member may sell, assign, transfer, pledge, encumber, hypothecate, or otherwise dispose of all or any portion of such Member\'s membership interest in the Company without the prior written consent of the Managing Member and Members holding at least seventy-five percent (75%) of the outstanding membership interests. Notwithstanding the foregoing, a Member may pledge such Member\'s membership interest to a lender as collateral for a bona fide loan, provided that such pledge has been approved in writing by the Managing Member. Any purported transfer in violation of this Section 9.1 shall be null and void and of no force or effect.

The Operating Agreement permits pledges of membership interests with Managing Member approval but does not distinguish between a pledge to the senior lender and a pledge to the mezzanine lender, nor does it address relative priority between competing pledges of the same membership interests. As noted in Section 1.2 above, the mezzanine lender (Brightleaf Mezzanine Capital LLC) currently holds a pledge of 100% of the membership interests in the Borrower as security for the mezzanine loan. If the senior construction lender, Pinnacle Savings Bank, N.A., also requires a pledge of 100% of the membership interests as collateral for the senior loan, the Operating Agreement provides no mechanism to resolve conflicting first-priority claims on the same collateral. The resolution of priority as between the competing pledges is expected to be addressed by the intercreditor agreement between Pinnacle Savings Bank, N.A. and Brightleaf Mezzanine Capital LLC, which has been negotiated but is not yet executed as of the date hereof.

**[SECTION 3: CERTIFICATION AND CONTACT INFORMATION]{.underline}**

The undersigned, as Managing Member of Harborview Capital Partners LLC, hereby certifies that the foregoing organizational chart is true, correct, and complete in all material respects as of the date hereof, and that the excerpts from the Operating Agreement set forth above are true, correct, and complete excerpts from the Amended and Restated Operating Agreement of Harborview Capital Partners LLC, dated as of March 14, 2019, as amended through December 1, 2024, as currently in effect. The undersigned further certifies that there have been no amendments to the Operating Agreement since December 1, 2024, and that no events have occurred since such date that would materially alter the organizational structure, membership interests, or governance provisions described herein.

from docx import Document
from docx.shared import Pt, Inches, RGBColor, Emu
from docx.enum.text import WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH, WD_LINE_SPACING, WD_TAB_ALIGNMENT
from docx.enum.table import WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT
from docx.enum.section import WD_SECTION
from docx.oxml.ns import qn
from docx.oxml import OxmlElement

NAVY = RGBColor(0x1F, 0x33, 0x53)
DARKRED = RGBColor(0x8B, 0x1A, 0x1A)
GREY = RGBColor(0x55, 0x55, 0x55)

def _set_cell_shading(cell, hexcolor):
    tcPr = cell._tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
    shd = OxmlElement('w:shd')
    shd.set(qn('w:val'), 'clear'); shd.set(qn('w:color'), 'auto'); shd.set(qn('w:fill'), hexcolor)
    tcPr.append(shd)

def _set_cell_margins(table, top=40, bottom=40, left=80, right=80):
    tblPr = table._tbl.tblPr
    mar = OxmlElement('w:tblCellMar')
    for k, v in (('top', top), ('left', left), ('bottom', bottom), ('right', right)):
        e = OxmlElement('w:' + k); e.set(qn('w:w'), str(v)); e.set(qn('w:type'), 'dxa'); mar.append(e)
    tblPr.append(mar)

def _borders(table, sz=4, color="808080"):
    tblPr = table._tbl.tblPr
    borders = OxmlElement('w:tblBorders')
    for edge in ('top', 'left', 'bottom', 'right', 'insideH', 'insideV'):
        e = OxmlElement('w:' + edge)
        e.set(qn('w:val'), 'single'); e.set(qn('w:sz'), str(sz)); e.set(qn('w:space'), '0'); e.set(qn('w:color'), color)
        borders.append(e)
    tblPr.append(borders)

def _keep_next(paragraph):
    pPr = paragraph._p.get_or_add_pPr()
    k = OxmlElement('w:keepNext'); pPr.append(k)

def new_doc(body_size=11, margins=(1.0, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0), font="Times New Roman"):
    doc = Document()
    st = doc.styles['Normal']
    st.font.name = font
    st.font.size = Pt(body_size)
    rpr = st.element.get_or_add_rPr()
    rf = rpr.find(qn('w:rFonts'))
    if rf is None:
        rf = OxmlElement('w:rFonts'); rpr.append(rf)
    for a in ('w:ascii', 'w:hAnsi', 'w:cs', 'w:eastAsia'):
        rf.set(qn(a), font)
    pf = st.paragraph_format
    pf.space_before = Pt(0); pf.space_after = Pt(8)
    pf.line_spacing_rule = WD_LINE_SPACING.SINGLE
    s = doc.sections[0]
    s.top_margin = Inches(margins[0]); s.right_margin = Inches(margins[1])
    s.bottom_margin = Inches(margins[2]); s.left_margin = Inches(margins[3])
    return doc

def add_field(paragraph, instr, font=None, size=None, bold=False):
    run = paragraph.add_run()
    f1 = OxmlElement('w:fldChar'); f1.set(qn('w:fldCharType'), 'begin')
    it = OxmlElement('w:instrText'); it.set(qn('xml:space'), 'preserve'); it.text = instr
    f2 = OxmlElement('w:fldChar'); f2.set(qn('w:fldCharType'), 'end')
    run._r.append(f1); run._r.append(it); run._r.append(f2)
    if font: run.font.name = font
    if size: run.font.size = Pt(size)
    run.bold = bold
    return run

def header_footer(doc, left_hdr, right_hdr, foot_left, size=8):
    sec = doc.sections[0]
    sec.different_first_page_header_footer = True
    hp = sec.header.paragraphs[0]
    hp.text = ""
    hp.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(2)
    hp.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.LEFT
    r = hp.add_run(left_hdr); r.font.size = Pt(size); r.font.color.rgb = GREY; r.font.name = "Times New Roman"
    pPr = hp._p.get_or_add_pPr()
    pbd = OxmlElement('w:pBdr'); b = OxmlElement('w:bottom')
    b.set(qn('w:val'), 'single'); b.set(qn('w:sz'), '4'); b.set(qn('w:space'), '1'); b.set(qn('w:color'), 'BFBFBF')
    pbd.append(b); pPr.append(pbd)

    fp = sec.footer.paragraphs[0]
    fp.text = ""
    fp.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
    r = fp.add_run(foot_left + "   |   Page "); r.font.size = Pt(size); r.font.color.rgb = GREY
    add_field(fp, " PAGE ", size=size, bold=False)
    r = fp.add_run(" of "); r.font.size = Pt(size); r.font.color.rgb = GREY
    add_field(fp, " NUMPAGES ", size=size)
    for run in fp.runs:
        run.font.name = "Times New Roman"; run.font.size = Pt(size); run.font.color.rgb = GREY

def title_block(doc, lines):
    for text, size, bold, space in lines:
        p = doc.add_paragraph()
        p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
        p.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(space[0]); p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(space[1])
        r = p.add_run(text); r.bold = bold; r.font.size = Pt(size)
        r.font.color.rgb = NAVY

def article(doc, num, name, page_break=True):
    if page_break:
        doc.add_page_break()
    p = doc.add_paragraph()
    p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
    p.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(0); p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(2)
    r = p.add_run(num); r.bold = True; r.font.size = Pt(11); r.font.color.rgb = NAVY
    p2 = doc.add_paragraph()
    p2.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
    p2.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(12)
    r2 = p2.add_run(name.upper()); r2.bold = True; r2.font.size = Pt(11); r2.font.color.rgb = NAVY
    _keep_next(p); _keep_next(p2)

def section(doc, num, caption):
    p = doc.add_paragraph()
    p.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(10); p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(4)
    p.paragraph_format.keep_with_next = True
    r = p.add_run("Section %s" % num)
    r.bold = True
    r2 = p.add_run("\u2003%s" % caption)
    r2.bold = True
    return p

def para(doc, text, indent=0.0, first=0.0, align="just", size=None, space_after=8, italic=False, bold_lead=None):
    p = doc.add_paragraph()
    pf = p.paragraph_format
    pf.left_indent = Inches(indent)
    pf.first_line_indent = Inches(first)
    pf.space_after = Pt(space_after)
    if align == "just":
        p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.JUSTIFY
    elif align == "center":
        p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
    else:
        p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.LEFT
    if bold_lead:

section(doc, "4.2", "Advances Are Not a Waiver.")
para(doc, "The making of any Advance shall not constitute a waiver of any condition to any subsequent Advance, nor a waiver of any Default or Event of Default, whether known or unknown to Lender, nor an approval of any work, materials, or Change Order not theretofore approved in writing by Lender.")

section(doc, "4.3", "Restricted Area Holdback.")
para(doc, "Notwithstanding any other provision of this Agreement, Lender shall not be obligated to make any Advance (or any portion of an Advance) allocable to the design, construction, or improvement of any portion of the Improvements located within or directly above the Restricted Area, and Borrower shall not permit any residential unit, residential common area, or other residential occupancy space to be constructed, marketed, leased, or occupied within or above the Restricted Area, unless and until one of the following has occurred and Lender has received evidence thereof reasonably satisfactory to it: (a) NCDEQ has issued a written modification to the NFA Letter approving residential use of the Restricted Area, subject to the installation, operation, and maintenance of the soil vapor mitigation system and such other conditions as NCDEQ may impose; (b) the Approved Plans and Specifications have been revised, with Lender\u2019s written consent, to eliminate residential use within and above the Restricted Area, and Borrower has delivered updated pro forma income projections reflecting such revision; or (c) Borrower has delivered a written determination from NCDEQ, in form and substance acceptable to Lender, confirming that residential use of the floors above the Restricted Area is permitted provided that the soil vapor mitigation system is installed, operating, and maintained in accordance with the NFA Letter.")
para(doc, "Borrower acknowledges that the Approved Plans and Specifications referenced in the Phase I ESA (drawing set dated September 12, 2024 prepared by Architect) depict approximately fourteen (14) residential units above the Restricted Area, and that no evidence has been provided to Lender that NCDEQ has approved such use. Borrower further acknowledges that the environmental consultant has expressly declined to verify the spatial relationship between the Restricted Area and any proposed residential occupancy space, and that the Appraisal expressly assumes Borrower will obtain any modification, variance, or approval necessary to permit the planned use at Borrower\u2019s sole cost.")
draftnote(doc, "This is the single most important unresolved environmental issue in the file. Credit Memorandum Section 9.5 estimates that losing 14 units reduces stabilized NOI from $4,876,800 to $4,499,640 and reduces DSCR from 1.31x to 1.21x, below the 1.25x minimum, and observes that the Appraisal does not adjust value for the restriction. Because the delineation in Figure 3 to the Phase I ESA is described on an orientation (Foster Street \u201cto the north\u201d) that is inconsistent with the recorded legal descriptions (Foster Street lies along the western boundary), the affected area must be re-plotted against the Survey before the holdback can be administered. See Cover Memorandum Items D-1 and E-4.")

article(doc, "ARTICLE 5", "Disbursement, Project Budget, Retainage and Cost Overruns")

section(doc, "5.1", "Advances in Accordance with Draw Schedule.")
para(doc, "Advances shall be made in accordance with the milestone draw schedule set forth on Schedule 4, subject to the conditions of Article 4. Lender shall use commercially reasonable efforts to process each complete Draw Request within ten (10) Business Days after Lender\u2019s receipt of a complete Draw Request and all required supporting documentation. Lender may, in its reasonable discretion, make Advances more or less frequently than indicated in Schedule 4, in each case consistent with the total amount of the Commitment and the conditions of this Agreement. The amount of any Advance may not exceed the lesser of (a) the amount requested in the applicable Draw Request and (b) the amount then available under the Approved Budget for the applicable budget line item, net of Retainage.")

section(doc, "5.2", "Draw Requests.")
para(doc, "Each Draw Request shall be submitted substantially in the form of Exhibit B, shall be signed by an authorized representative of Borrower, and shall include: (a) AIA Documents G702 (Application and Certificate for Payment) and G703 (Continuation Sheet), certified by Contractor and Architect; (b) the Requisition Certificate; (c) the Construction Inspector\u2019s report; (d) conditional and unconditional lien waivers as required by Section 4.1(e); (e) the title date-down endorsement required by Section 4.1(f); (f) evidence of insurance; (g) an updated construction schedule and change order log; (h) an updated sources and uses reconciliation; (i) the Interest Reserve Adequacy Certificate; and (j) such other information as Lender may reasonably require. Lender may decline to fund any Draw Request that is incomplete or that does not satisfy the conditions of Article 4.")

section(doc, "5.3", "Retainage.")
para(doc, "Lender shall withhold Retainage equal to ten percent (10%) of each Advance allocable to Hard Costs, and shall not disburse such Retainage except in accordance with Section 5.8. The aggregate Retainage on the Guaranteed Maximum Price of $34,750,000 is $3,475,000. Borrower shall cause Contractor to acknowledge the Retainage in the Construction Contract and in each Application for Payment, and no Advance shall be deemed to approve or accept any work in a manner that would limit Lender\u2019s right to withhold or recover Retainage. The Retainage shall be held by Lender (and not by Borrower or Contractor) and shall not be subject to any Lien of Contractor, any subcontractor, or any other Person.")
para(doc, "Borrower acknowledges that the draw schedule attached as Schedule 4 to the Term Sheet (and the Borrower-prepared draw schedule dated January 8, 2025 delivered to Lender) provides for each hard-cost draw to be funded at one hundred percent (100%) of the gross amount requested and then provides for a further \u201cRetainage Release\u201d draw following the certificate of occupancy, which would result in cumulative hard-cost disbursements of $38,225,000 against a Guaranteed Maximum Price of $34,750,000, an over-advance of $3,475,000. Schedule 4 to this Agreement restates the draw schedule to withhold Retainage from each Advance in accordance with this Section 5.3.")
draftnote(doc, "This paragraph records the discrepancy on the face of the Borrower\u2019s draw schedule so that it cannot later be characterized as a Lender-approved funding mechanism. Note that the Borrower\u2019s schedule also purports to fund $2,835,000 of Developer Fee and $1,440,000 of Contingency within the same draw lines, which is what creates the appearance of reconciliation. See Cover Memorandum Item F-1 for the full recomputation.")

section(doc, "5.4", "Equity First; Equity Escrow Account.")
para(doc, "Before any Advance other than the Initial Advance is made, the Equity Contribution shall have been deposited into the Equity Escrow Account and applied to Project Costs. Funds in the Equity Escrow Account shall be disbursed to pay Project Costs in the priority set forth in the Equity Escrow Agreement and shall be exhausted before any Loan proceeds are applied to the same Project Costs. Borrower shall not be entitled to any credit against the Commitment on account of the Equity Contribution, and no Advance shall be made if the making of such Advance would cause the Loan-to-Cost Ratio to exceed the maximum set forth in Section 9.1.")

section(doc, "5.5", "Interest Reserve.")
sub(doc, "(a)", "Establishment and Funding. Lender shall fund the Interest Reserve of $4,850,000 from Loan proceeds with the Initial Advance and shall hold the Interest Reserve in a segregated sub-account of the Loan (the \u201cInterest Reserve Account\u201d), which shall not constitute a deposit account of Borrower and shall bear no interest.")
sub(doc, "(b)", "Application. sub(doc, "(c)", "Sole Source; No Reallocation. The Interest Reserve shall be used solely for the payment of interest and Other Charges during the Construction Period and may not be reallocated to any other budget line item, whether by budget modification, Change Order, or otherwise. Amounts remaining in the Interest Reserve Account after the Construction Maturity Date shall be applied to the outstanding principal balance of the Loan.")
sub(doc, "(d)", "Interest Reserve Adequacy Test. At each Draw Request and at least quarterly during the Construction Period, Borrower shall deliver to Lender an Interest Reserve Adequacy Certificate substantially in the form of Exhibit D, certified by the chief financial officer of Borrower, demonstrating that the remaining balance of the Interest Reserve Account, together with any additional funds Borrower has committed in writing to deposit, is sufficient to pay all projected interest on the Loan (calculated at the greater of the then-current Applicable Rate and the Applicable Rate assuming Daily Simple SOFR of 4.35%) through the earlier of (i) the next anticipated draw date and (ii) the date that is ninety (90) days after the date of such certificate. If the Interest Reserve Adequacy Test is not satisfied, Borrower shall deposit the amount of the deficiency into the Interest Reserve Account within five (5) Business Days after written demand by Lender, and no further Advance shall be made until such deposit is made.")
sub(doc, "(e)", "Replenishment; Shortfall. Borrower shall fund any shortfall in the Interest Reserve from its own funds (and not from Loan proceeds, Mezzanine Loan proceeds, or the proceeds of any other Indebtedness) within five (5) Business Days after written notice from Lender. Failure to fund any such shortfall within such period shall constitute an Event of Default under Section 15.1(a).")
sub(doc, "(f)", "Reporting. Borrower shall deliver to Lender, concurrently with each monthly construction progress report, a reconciliation of the Interest Reserve Account showing the opening balance, interest and Other Charges paid, deposits made, and closing balance, together with a projection of remaining interest costs through the Construction Maturity Date.")
draftnote(doc, "Reserve sizing is not settled in the record. The Term Sheet and Credit Memorandum fix the Interest Reserve at $4,850,000. The Credit Memorandum (Section 6.2) computes a shortfall of approximately $565,000 at a 7.60% all-in rate on an assumed $28,500,000 average outstanding balance. The Borrower\u2019s January 8, 2025 model computes a shortfall of $365,830 at the same 7.60% rate but concludes \u201cAPPEARS ADEQUATE\u201d because its headline case assumes SOFR of 3.50% (all-in 6.75%) rather than the 4.35% current rate used in the Credit Memorandum. Architectural Review Committee, without the prior written consent of Lender in each case. Borrower shall deliver an updated change order log with each Draw Request and with each monthly construction progress report.")
