{"command": "cd $WORKSPACE_DIR/build && cat >> build_memo.py <<'PYEOF'

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 4
PRI_COLOR = {"Critical": DARKRED, "High": RGBColor(0x9A, 0x5B, 0x00), "Medium": RGBColor(0x1F, 0x33, 0x53), "Low": GREY}

def issue(code, title, pri, blocks):
    p = doc.add_paragraph()
    p.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(11); p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(3)
    p.paragraph_format.keep_with_next = True
    r = p.add_run("%s.  %s" % (code, title)); r.bold = True; r.font.size = Pt(10.5)
    r2 = p.add_run("   [%s]" % pri); r2.bold = True; r2.font.size = Pt(8.5); r2.font.color.rgb = PRI_COLOR[pri]
    for label, text in blocks:
        q = doc.add_paragraph()
        q.paragraph_format.left_indent = Inches(0.3)
        q.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(4)
        q.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.JUSTIFY
        rl = q.add_run(label + "  "); rl.bold = True; rl.font.size = Pt(9.8); rl.italic = True
        rt = q.add_run(text); rt.font.size = Pt(9.8)

h1(doc, "4.  MATERIAL ISSUES AND RECOMMENDED RESOLUTIONS")
para(doc, "Each issue below identifies the source documents and provisions in conflict, states the discrepancy as we recomputed it, explains why it matters to the credit or the collateral position, and recommends a resolution. \u201cWhere addressed\u201d identifies the section of the draft Loan Agreement that implements the recommendation.")

h2(doc, "A.  Capital structure, equity and leverage", size=11.5)

issue("A-1", "The Loan cannot satisfy its own 80% loan-to-cost covenant, and the proposed equity escrow does not cure the breach", "Critical", [
 ("Sources.", "Term Sheet \u00a7 6.1 (maximum LTC 80% of Total Project Costs, tested \u201cat any time during the term\u201d), \u00a7 5.2 (Total Project Costs $56,700,000) and \u00a7 3.1 (Loan Amount $47,500,000); Credit Memorandum \u00a7 5.3 and \u00a7 6.1 (LTC 83.77%, reported as \u201cFail\u201d) and \u00a7 10.1.2 (condition of approval: deposit of $2,140,000 in cash into a Bank-controlled equity escrow)."),
 ("Discrepancy.", "$47,500,000 \u00f7 $56,700,000 = 83.774%. At an 80% maximum, Total Project Costs of $56,700,000 support a senior loan of $45,360,000, so the Loan exceeds the covenant by $2,140,000 (3.77 percentage points). The Credit Memorandum acknowledges the exceedance but proposes an equity escrow as the cure. An escrow deposit changes neither the numerator (the Loan Amount) nor the denominator (Total Project Costs), so the ratio remains 83.77% after the deposit. The escrow would only affect the ratio if (a) the Loan Amount were correspondingly reduced, or (b) Total Project Costs were increased by the amount of additional costs the equity funds, which requires Total Project Costs of $59,375,000 ($47,500,000 \u00f7 0.80) \u2014 a $2,675,000 increase."),
 ("Impact.", "The covenant is breached on the Closing Date and at all times thereafter, including at substantial completion when the Loan is fully drawn. The compliance certificate required as a closing condition (drafted at \u00a7 3.1(w)) cannot be given truthfully, and every draw condition that incorporates the LTC test is unsatisfiable. A lender that closes a loan knowing a financial covenant is breached, and later declares a default on that covenant, faces waiver, estoppel and lender-liability arguments, and an examiner would treat it as an unapproved policy exception."),
 ("Recommendation.", "We recommend one of two resolutions, in order of preference. (1) Reduce the Commitment to $45,360,000 and require a verified cash Equity Contribution of $2,140,000, bringing sources to $45,360,000 + $9,200,000 + $2,140,000 = $56,700,000. This is the only arithmetic cure that preserves the 80% policy limit, it matches the $2,140,000 the Credit Memorandum already conditioned, and it forces real cash into the structure. (2) Retain the Loan at $47,500,000 and increase Total Project Costs to not less than $59,375,000 by adding the omitted items identified in Issue F-2 (which we estimate at not less than $1.7 million) and the interest reserve increase in Issue H-1 (approximately $750,000), funding the increment with verified cash equity of not less than $2,675,000. Option (2) also improves the LTV, funds the omitted costs, and enlarges the interest reserve. If the Committee elects to keep the Loan at $47,500,000 without new equity, it should record an express policy exception at 83.77% and conform \u00a7 6.1 of the Term Sheet and the compliance certificate, and it should expect to defend the exception at the next examination."),
 ("Where addressed.", "\u00a7 2.1 (automatic commitment reduction), \u00a7 5.4 (equity first), \u00a7 9.1 (covenant with the arithmetic disclosed), Schedule 3 Part 2, and Schedule 5."),
])

issue("A-2", "As-completed loan-to-value is 65.25% against a 65% maximum, and the Credit Memorandum silently applies a 70% policy maximum", "Critical", [
 ("Sources.", "Term Sheet \u00a7 4 (\u201cThe Lender\u2019s maximum loan-to-value ratio shall not exceed 65% on an as-completed basis\u201d) and \u00a7 6.2 (65% as-completed and 65% as-stabilized); Credit Memorandum \u00a7 6.1 (LTV as-completed 65.25%, \u201cBank Policy\u201d shown as \u201cMax 70%\u201d, status \u201cPass\u201d)."),
 ("Discrepancy.", "$47,500,000 \u00f7 $72,800,000 = 65.247%. 65% of $72,800,000 is $47,320,000, so the Loan exceeds the as-completed LTV cap by $180,000. The Credit Memorandum measures the ratio against a 70% maximum that does not appear in the Term Sheet and does not disclose the substitution. The as-stabilized ratio (62.34% against 65%) is compliant."),
 ("Impact.", "This is a second covenant breached at closing. It also reveals that the Term Sheet and the credit approval are applying different credit policies to the same loan, which is the kind of inconsistency that produces findings in an OCC commercial real estate portfolio review."),
 ("Recommendation.", "Conform both documents to the Term Sheet\u2019s 65% maximum. If resolution (1) in Issue A-1 is adopted, the $45,360,000 commitment produces an as-completed LTV of 62.31% and this issue disappears. If the Loan remains at $47,500,000, either the Commitment must be reduced by $180,000 to $47,320,000 or the Committee must approve 65.25% as an exception and confirm which policy maximum governs."),
 ("Where addressed.", "\u00a7 9.2 (covenant retained at 65%, with the computation disclosed) and Schedule 5."),
])

issue("A-3", "The land is not Borrower equity: the Borrower\u2019s own budget funds the $8,200,000 land cost from Mezzanine Loan proceeds", "Critical", [
 ("Sources.", "Term Sheet \u00a7 5.1 (\u201cBorrower Equity (land previously acquired): $0\u201d) and \u00a7 5.2 (\u201cThe land \u2026 is contributed to the Project as the Borrower\u2019s equity\u201d); Credit Memorandum \u00a7 5.1 (\u201cThe land acquisition cost of $8,200,000 was funded from prior capital calls from members, including contributions from Brightleaf Investors Group LLC\u201d) and \u00a7 9.1 (\u201cthe land \u2026 providing embedded equity\u201d); Borrower\u2019s Detailed Budget, line 1.01 (\u201cLand Acquisition \u2026 Funded by Mezzanine Loan $8,200,000\u201d; note: \u201cPreviously closed; funded by mezzanine loan proceeds and member capital calls\u201d); Organizational Chart \u00a7 1.3 (\u201cTotal member equity to date: $8,200,000\u201d; \u201cBrightleaf Investors Group LLC: $0 cash to date\u201d)."),
 ("Discrepancy.", "The documents cannot all be correct. The Term Sheet treats the land as contributed equity but shows Borrower equity of $0. The Credit Memorandum treats the land as the only equity and says it was funded by capital calls from all three members. The Organizational Chart says it was contributed solely by Ms. Vasquez-Torres, with the other two members contributing nothing. The Borrower\u2019s own budget says the $8,200,000 land cost is funded by Mezzanine Loan proceeds. On the Borrower\u2019s own allocation, senior debt of $47,500,000 plus mezzanine debt of $9,200,000 equals Total Project Costs of $56,700,000 exactly \u2014 100% leverage with no equity anywhere in the stack."),
 ("Impact.", "This is the central credit issue in the file. It means the Bank\u2019s protection is value-based only: the entire $56,700,000 of cost is debt, so any decline in value from cost places the senior lender in a loss position, and the sponsor has no cash at risk and therefore no economic incentive to fund overruns or an interest shortfall. It also converts the mezzanine position from subordinated debt into what is functionally a refinancing of the sponsor\u2019s land basis. Finally, if the Borrower fails within the applicable look-back period, a trustee would examine the land valuation, the contribution, and the $9,200,000 distribution to the sponsor\u2019s benefit as potential constructive-fraud or preference transfers."),
 ("Recommendation.", "(1) Require a traced source-of-funds schedule supported by bank records and the closing statement for the 2023 acquisition, identifying precisely who paid the $8,200,000 and when. (2) Require the $2,140,000 verified cash Equity Contribution, with a lender-controlled escrow and a source certification that excludes the mezzanine lender, Brightleaf Investors Group LLC, and Mr. Chen (already drafted at \u00a7 3.1(b)). (3) Prohibit application of any Mezzanine Loan proceeds to land reimbursement or to any fee payable to the Borrower or its members, and consider requiring that the mezzanine proceeds be deposited with the Bank and applied solely to construction costs. (4) Require a solvency certificate and a fraudulent-transfer opinion from Borrower\u2019s counsel at closing."),
 ("Where addressed.", "\u00a7 5.4, \u00a7 5.13 (Developer Fee), \u00a7 18.3 (mezzanine fees and distributions), Schedule 3 Parts 2 and 3, and Schedule 3-A."),
])

issue("A-4", "$1,000,000 of the Developer Fee is funded from Mezzanine Loan proceeds at closing", "High", [
 ("Sources.", "Borrower\u2019s Detailed Budget, line 5.01 (Developer Fee $2,835,000: $1,835,000 senior, $1,000,000 mezzanine); Term Sheet \u00a7 14 (no Distributions during the Construction Period other than the Developer Fee) and \u00a7 5.2 (Developer Fee as a use of funds)."),
 ("Discrepancy.", "The Developer Fee is a payment to the Borrower, which is owned by the same individuals who guarantee the Loan. Funding it with borrowed money at closing is a distribution of loan proceeds to the sponsor \u2014 economically identical to a dividend \u2014 and it is the second component (with the land reimbursement) of the $9,200,000 of mezzanine proceeds that reaches the sponsor rather than the Project. None of the $9,200,000 of mezzanine money is applied to construction."),
 ("Impact.", "The Bank finances the sponsor\u2019s fee at closing, which reduces the equity cushion to zero and increases the amount at risk. If the Project fails, the Bank will be met with the argument that $1,000,000 of the proceeds was paid out to the Borrower rather than invested in the collateral."),
 ("Recommendation.", "Defer the Developer Fee in its entirety. Permit payment only from demonstrated cost savings after all hard costs, soft costs, and reserves are funded, in installments, with no Default and no projected overrun, and subject to the Bank\u2019s right to redirect it to cure an overrun or an interest shortfall (drafted). Delete the $1,000,000 mezzanine allocation; if the arithmetic requires that $1,000,000 to be funded by someone, it should be funded by verified equity, not by the mezzanine lender."),
 ("Where addressed.", "\u00a7 5.13 and \u00a7 18.3; the Developer Fee is also removed from the Retainage Release line in Schedule 4."),

issue("A-6", "The sources and uses statement foots only because the $8,200,000 land use has no corresponding source", "High", [
 ("Sources.", "Term Sheet \u00a7\u00a7 5.1\u20135.2; Credit Memorandum \u00a7\u00a7 5.1\u20135.2; Borrower\u2019s \u201cSummary\u201d tab."),

 ("Where addressed.", "Schedule 3 Parts 1 and 2."),

issue("A-7", "The equity escrow leaves $2,140,000 of undrawn commitment available to be drawn later, restoring 83.77% leverage", "High", [

h2(doc, "B.  Borrower financial strength", size=11.5)

h2(doc, "C.  Membership interests, pledges, guaranties and control", size=11.5)
issue("C-1", "Both loans are documented as holding a first-priority pledge of 100% of the membership interests", "Critical", [
 ("Sources.", "Term Sheet \u00a7 8 (pledge of 100% of membership interests as senior collateral) and \u00a7 1.4 (mezzanine loan \u201csecured by a pledge of 100% of the membership interests\u201d); Credit Memorandum \u00a7 4.2 and \u00a7 9.4 (identifies the conflict; recommends senior first priority, mezzanine second); Organizational Chart \u00a7 1.2 and \u00a7 2.5 (mezzanine lender \u201ccurrently holds a pledge of 100% of the membership interests\u201d; the operating agreement has no priority mechanism)."),
 ("Discrepancy.", "Two lenders cannot each hold a first-priority security interest in the same collateral.  ("Impact.", "Absent a signed intercreditor agreement, the Bank does not have the collateral position its approval describes, and a default would produce a priority contest at the worst possible time. There are also two practical problems that the Credit Memorandum does not address. First, perfection against individual pledgors requires UCC-1 filings not with the Secretary of State but with the register of deeds of the county of each individual\u2019s residence (Durham County for Ms. Vasquez-Torres, Orange County for Mr. Osei), while the LLC pledgor (Brightleaf Investors Group LLC) requires Secretary of State filing.  ("Recommendation.", "Adopt the Credit Memorandum\u2019s preferred structure \u2014 senior first priority, mezzanine second \u2014 and implement it properly: (a) amend the operating agreement to provide for certificated membership interests and to authorize the pledges expressly; (b) require delivery of the original certificates with undated transfer powers in favor of the Bank; (c) file UCC-1s in the correct offices for each pledgor (and obtain UCC-3 subordination of the mezzanine lender\u2019s filings); (d) obtain an account control agreement over any distribution account; (e) provide that voting rights pass to the Bank only after a default; and (f) if the intercreditor agreement cannot be executed by the closing date, fall back to the Credit Memorandum\u2019s alternative of relying on the real property collateral alone and delete the pledge from the collateral package so that the documents match the deal."),
 ("Where addressed.", "\u00a7 13.1 (collateral), \u00a7 18.2 (intercreditor as a non-waivable condition), and \u00a7 3.1(c)."),
])

issue("C-2", "The pledge requires the consent of the member whose affiliate holds the competing pledge", "High", [
 ("Sources.", "Organizational Chart \u00a7 2.5 (Operating Agreement \u00a7 9.1: no pledge of a membership interest without the written consent of the Managing Member and members holding 75%); \u00a7 2.2 (Operating Agreement \u00a7 3.2: 75% approval for any financing over $1,000,000 and for any amendment)."),
 ("Discrepancy.", "A first-priority pledge to the Bank requires the consent of members holding 75% \u2014 which necessarily includes Brightleaf Investors Group LLC, whose affiliate is the mezzanine lender that would be subordinated by that consent.  ("Impact.", "A closing condition is controlled by the subordinate lender\u2019s affiliate. If that consent is conditioned or delayed, closing fails; if it is given informally, the pledge may be voidable."),
 ("Recommendation.", "Obtain executed, unconditional written consents from all three members at or before closing, and an amendment to the operating agreement (approved by 75% of the members) that (a) authorizes the senior pledge as a permitted pledge with first priority, (b) waives the consent requirements for the Loan Documents and all actions required thereunder, and (c) adds the Independent Manager and separateness covenants."),
 ("Where addressed.", "\u00a7 3.1(n) and \u00a7 8.1(e)."),
])

issue("C-3", "A 75% supermajority gives the mezzanine lender\u2019s affiliate a veto over bankruptcy, refinancing and any amendment", "Critical", [
 ("Sources.", "Organizational Chart \u00a7 2.2 (Operating Agreement \u00a7 3.2), and the Organizational Chart\u2019s own analysis: Ms. Vasquez-Torres (62%) plus Mr. Osei (10%) hold 72%, below the 75% threshold, so \u201cBrightleaf Investors Group LLC holds an effective veto right over major decisions\u201d; Credit Memorandum \u00a7 9.3 (independent manager as \u201cthe single most important structural safeguard against a bad-faith bankruptcy filing\u201d)."),
 ("Discrepancy.", "The Credit Memorandum assumes that an independent manager will control the bankruptcy decision. Under the operating agreement as it exists, a voluntary bankruptcy filing requires 75% member approval, which cannot be obtained without Brightleaf Investors Group LLC \u2014 an affiliate of the mezzanine lender through Mr. Chen. The same 75% threshold governs any refinancing over $1,000,000, any amendment to the operating agreement (including the SPE amendments the Bank requires as a condition of closing), any admission of a new member, and any sale of the Project."),
 ("Impact.", "The bankruptcy-remoteness structure the Bank is paying for does not exist: the party that decides whether the Borrower files is an affiliate of the subordinate lender, whose interests in a workout diverge from the Bank\u2019s. The Bank also cannot compel the Borrower to amend its operating agreement without the affiliate\u2019s consent, and cannot obtain a consensual refinancing or sale in a workout without it."),
 ("Recommendation.", "Amend the operating agreement, with 75% approval obtained as a closing condition, so that (a) the bankruptcy and insolvency decisions rest solely with the Independent Manager, (b) member approval is not required for any action required under the Loan Documents, (c) the 75% threshold does not apply to a refinancing with, or a sale approved by, the Bank, and (d) Brightleaf Investors Group LLC delivers an irrevocable proxy or a direct consent agreement enforceable by the Bank. If Brightleaf will not consent, the Bank should treat the SPE structure as unavailable and re-price or decline."),
 ("Where addressed.", "\u00a7 11.6 (Independent Manager), \u00a7 8.1(e) (operating agreement amendments), \u00a7 3.1(n), and \u00a7 15.1(p)."),
])

issue("C-4", "A 28% equity holder contributed no capital, holds a blocking vote, and controls the mezzanine lender", "High", [
 ("Sources.", "Organizational Chart \u00a7 1.3 and \u00a7 2.3 (Brightleaf Investors Group LLC \u201cshall make an initial capital contribution of Zero Dollars ($0)\u201d in consideration of \u201cits commitment to arrange third-party mezzanine financing\u201d); Credit Memorandum \u00a7 2.2, \u00a7 4.4 and \u00a7 9.3 (common control through Mr. Chen; substantive consolidation risk)."),
 ("Discrepancy.", "The 28% member\u2019s economic return comes from mezzanine interest (12.50% fixed, paid-in-kind during construction per the Credit Memorandum), not from residual equity. Its capital contribution is zero, it is not a guarantor, and it holds the swing vote on major decisions. Economically this is closer to a preferred-return joint venture partner than to a lender behind a common equity holder."),
 ("Impact.", "The Bank\u2019s subordinate lender and blocking equity holder are the same economic actor. In a workout, that actor\u2019s return is maximized by protecting its 12.50% position rather than the collateral, and its consent will be required for any restructuring."),
 ("Recommendation.", "Require one of: (a) an equity commitment letter from Brightleaf Investors Group LLC obligating it to fund its pro rata share (28%) of capital calls and cost overruns, secured by a pledge of its membership interest; (b) a springing guaranty from Mr. Chen or Brightleaf for a defined amount; or (c) re-underwriting that treats the mezzanine as equity, which would reduce the senior loan to a loan-to-cost of approximately 65% of the combined capital. Also obtain a substantive consolidation analysis (the non-consolidation opinion required at \u00a7 3.1(o)) addressed specifically to the Brightleaf entities."),
 ("Where addressed.", "Article 18, \u00a7 8.1(f) (affiliate transactions), and \u00a7 3.1(o)."),
])

issue("C-5", "The partial repayment guaranty equals 103.3% of one guarantor\u2019s net worth and exceeds both guarantors\u2019 liquid assets combined", "Medium", [
 ("Sources.", "Term Sheet \u00a7\u00a7 1.3, 6.5 and 7.3; Credit Memorandum \u00a7 2.3.3."),
 ("Discrepancy.", "Each guarantor is jointly and severally liable for $11,875,000. Against Mr. Osei\u2019s $11,500,000 net worth (of which $6,800,000 is real estate and only $3,200,000 is liquid), the guaranty equals 103.3% of net worth and 371% of his liquid assets. Combined liquid assets are $9,300,000, which is less than the $11,875,000 guaranteed amount. Because the same liquidity must satisfy the $5,000,000 covenant, a guaranty call and a covenant breach would occur simultaneously."),
 ("Impact.", "Recovery on the partial guaranty in a default is realistically limited to liquid assets of roughly $9,300,000, and collection would require litigation against two individuals over illiquid real estate."),
 ("Recommendation.", "Consider a per-guarantor liability cap tied to verified liquid assets (for example, $6,000,000 for Ms. Vasquez-Torres and $3,500,000 for Mr. Osei, in the aggregate not exceeding $11,875,000), or accept the joint and several structure and rely on the completion and carry guaranties for the construction risk. In either case obtain current personal financial statements, two years of tax returns, and a credit report for each guarantor before closing, and require the liquidity certificate to exclude pledged and non-marketable assets (drafted at \u00a7 9.5)."),
 ("Where addressed.", "\u00a7 14.3, \u00a7 9.5, and \u00a7 3.1(q)."),
])

issue("C-6", "The aggregate amount of the partial repayment guaranty is ambiguous", "Medium", [
 ("Sources.", "Term Sheet \u00a7 7.3 (\u201cin the amount of 25% of the Loan Amount (25% \u00d7 $47,500,000 = $11,875,000) \u2026 joint and several, meaning that each Guarantor shall be individually liable for the full guaranteed amount\u201d); Credit Memorandum \u00a7 4.3 (\u201c$11,875,000 per guarantor\u201d)."),
 ("Discrepancy.", "The phrase \u201ceach Guarantor shall be individually liable for the full guaranteed amount\u201d can be read as $11,875,000 per guarantor ($23,750,000 in the aggregate) or as $11,875,000 in the aggregate for which each is jointly and severally liable. The Credit Memorandum\u2019s \u201cper guarantor\u201d language supports the former; the 25%-of-Loan-Amount economic term supports the latter."),
 ("Impact.", "A court may construe the ambiguity against the drafter and enforce only the lower amount, or the Bank may under-collect. Either way the credit is not enforceable as approved."),
 ("Recommendation.", "State the aggregate cap expressly and provide that recoveries from the guarantors in the aggregate may not exceed $11,875,000 (drafted)."),
 ("Where addressed.", "\u00a7 14.3."),
])

h2(doc, "D.  Environmental matters", size=11.5)
issue("D-1", "The NCDEQ land use restriction prohibits residential use of 0.38 acres, and the plans place 14 residential units above that area", "Critical", [
 ("Sources.", "Phase I ESA \u00a7 1, \u00a7 7 (Condition 2) and \u00a7 8.5; Credit Memorandum \u00a7 8.2 and \u00a7 9.5 (quantifies the impact) and \u00a7 10.1.7; Term Sheet \u00a7 17; Appraisal \u00a7 8 and Extraordinary Assumption 7."),
 ("Discrepancy.", "The NFA Letter states that the NFA determination \u201cis contingent upon the restriction of future use of the affected area to non-residential (commercial or industrial) purposes\u201d and that any change to residential use \u201cwould require additional investigation and/or remediation \u2026 and a modification to this NFA determination would need to be obtained from NCDEQ prior to such change in use.\u201d The Credit Memorandum states that the plans place 14 residential units above that area. The Phase I ESA expressly declines to verify the overlay (because it requires the floor plans to be overlaid on the delineation map) and classifies the condition as a \u201cbusiness environmental risk.\u201d Two documents understate the problem: the Term Sheet \u00a7 17 recites only the vapor mitigation condition and does not mention the use restriction at all, and the Appraisal states that it has not adjusted value for the restriction and expresses no view on the legality of the residential use."),
 ("Impact.", "The Credit Memorandum\u2019s own arithmetic shows the effect: removing 14 units at the $2,245 average rent reduces stabilized NOI by $377,160 to $4,499,640 and reduces DSCR from 1.31x to 1.21x, below the 1.25x minimum. If the City refuses certificates of occupancy for those units, the Project cannot service the Loan at the underwritten coverage. The absence of any adjustment in the Appraisal means the as-completed value of $72,800,000 and the resulting 65.25% LTV may be overstated as well. There is also a documentation risk: because the Term Sheet recites only the vapor condition, the Borrower could later argue that the Bank knew of and accepted the residential program."),
 ("Recommendation.", "Resolve one of three ways before closing: (a) obtain an NCDEQ modification to the NFA Letter permitting residential use above the affected area subject to the vapor mitigation system; (b) redesign to eliminate residential occupancy above the Restricted Area and provide updated projections and an updated appraisal; or (c) obtain a written NCDEQ determination that residential use above the grade-level restricted area is permitted with engineering controls. If the Committee elects to defer (the Credit Memorandum would allow deferral to the advance stage), then: hold back all advances allocable to work within or above the Restricted Area (drafted), make occupancy of any residential space above the Restricted Area a draw condition, correct the Term Sheet \u00a7 17 recital in the definitive documents, and obtain an environmental counsel opinion on the scope of the restriction. We also recommend re-plotting the 0.38-acre delineation on the survey before the holdback is administered, because the Phase I ESA\u2019s site orientation conflicts with the recorded descriptions (Issue E-4)."),
 ("Where addressed.", "\u00a7 4.3 (Restricted Area holdback), \u00a7 8.1(j), \u00a7 10.2(b), \u00a7 10.5 (delineation), and Schedule 8."),
])

issue("D-2", "The deed notice required by the NFA Letter was due November 29, 2024, is not on the December 5, 2024 title commitment, and the Appraisal states that it is recorded", "Critical", [
 ("Sources.", "Phase I ESA \u00a7 7 (Condition 4: notice to be recorded within 60 days of September 30, 2024) and \u00a7 8.1 (\u201cthe required deed notice had not yet been recorded\u201d and the NFA conditions \u201chave not been fully implemented\u201d); Title Commitment Schedule B-II (no environmental declaration of land use restriction listed) and Note 5 (environmental matters outside the scope of the commitment); Appraisal \u00a7 8 (\u201cThis land use restriction is memorialized in a Declaration of Land Use Restrictions recorded at the Durham County Register of Deeds\u201d)."),
 ("Discrepancy.", "Three sources, three positions. The NFA Letter required recording by November 29, 2024. The consultant reported on October 28, 2024 that it had not been recorded. The title commitment effective December 5, 2024 \u2014 six days after the deadline \u2014 does not show it in Schedule B-II. The Appraisal asserts that it is recorded. Because a recorded land use restriction would appear as an exception on a title commitment covering the same registry, the Appraisal\u2019s statement is not supported by the record."),
 ("Impact.", "Either the Borrower failed a condition of its NFA determination, exposing the Project to a reopened regulatory file and to the loss of the closure that supports the entire development program, or the title commitment is incomplete. Either way the Bank is asked to fund against an environmental status it has not verified. A recorded restriction that is not a Permitted Exception would also be excepted from the title policy, with a corresponding effect on marketability and value."),
 ("Recommendation.", "Before closing: (a) obtain a current title bring-down and, if recorded, a copy of the instrument; (b) if not recorded, require recording before closing in a form acceptable to the Bank and to the title company, and obtain written NCDEQ confirmation that recording after the deadline does not impair the NFA determination; (c) add the recorded instrument to the Permitted Exceptions (drafted); and (d) require a specific representation as to the recordation status (drafted at \u00a7 6.1(o)(e)) so that the Bank\u2019s file records what was known at closing. The Appraisal\u2019s statement should be corrected by the appraiser or disregarded."),
 ("Where addressed.", "\u00a7 3.1(f), \u00a7 6.1(o), \u00a7 10.2(d), Schedule 2, and Schedule 8."),
])

issue("D-3", "The required soil vapor mitigation system has not been designed, is not separately costed, and carries a hard NCDEQ reporting deadline", "High", [
 ("Sources.", "Phase I ESA \u00a7 7 (Condition 1: passive sub-slab depressurization system designed by a North Carolina licensed professional engineer, with as-built drawings and a performance verification report submitted to NCDEQ within 90 days after completion of the building foundation); Borrower\u2019s Detailed Budget line 2.08 (\u201cIncludes soil vapor mitigation system per NCDEQ NFA requirements\u201d within the $3,590,000 parking structure line); Appraisal \u00a7 8 (states that the cost is included in the hard cost budget)."),
 ("Discrepancy.", "No design, specification, or separate cost appears anywhere in the record. The system cost is embedded in the parking structure line with no identified amount, so neither the Bank nor the inspector can verify that it is funded."),
 ("Impact.", "The 90-day post-foundation submission deadline will fall in the middle of construction, and failure to meet it is an NFA violation and a default. If the system is underfunded, the cost becomes a change order or an overrun funded by the guarantors."),
 ("Recommendation.", "Require the PE design and NCDEQ-compliant specification before closing, a separately identified budget line item (with confirmation that the $3,590,000 parking line includes it), incorporation into the GMP contract scope and the inspector\u2019s milestone checklist, and a draw condition tied to timely NCDEQ submission."),
 ("Where addressed.", "\u00a7 3.1(k), \u00a7 10.2(a), \u00a7 4.1(m), and Schedule 8."),
])

issue("D-4", "The NCDEQ-approved soil management plan must be in place before any subsurface work in the affected area, and NCDEQ review time is not in the schedule", "High", [
 ("Sources.", "Phase I ESA \u00a7 7 (Condition 3) and Recommendation 4; Term Sheet \u00a7 17 (silent); Credit Memorandum \u00a7 10.1.7 (silent)."),
 ("Discrepancy.", "The NFA Letter requires that a soil management plan be submitted to and approved by NCDEQ before any construction activity involving subsurface disturbance within the affected area. Construction of the podium and foundations will necessarily involve that disturbance, yet the plan is not in the record, is not a listed closing condition in the Term Sheet or the Credit Memorandum, and no approval timeline is built into the 30-month schedule."),
 ("Impact.", "A construction start that is otherwise ready can be delayed pending agency approval, which consumes schedule float against a construction maturity date that already precedes the projected completion date by three days (Issue G-1)."),
 ("Recommendation.", "Submit the plan now and make NCDEQ approval a closing condition; incorporate the plan into the GMP contract by change order; require written acknowledgment from the contractor and all subcontractors; and confirm that the baseline schedule reflects the approval timeline."),
 ("Where addressed.", "\u00a7 3.1(k), \u00a7 10.2(c), \u00a7 5.7(d), and Schedule 8."),

issue("E-1", "An unreleased 2018 deed of trust securing $3,400,000 remains of record, its balance is unknown, and there is no source of funds to pay it", "Critical", [
 ("Sources.", "Title Commitment Schedule B-I Requirement 4 and Schedule B-II Item 10, including the Title Officer\u2019s note that Borrower\u2019s counsel advised by letter dated November 22, 2024 that the debt \u201chas been partially repaid and that the remaining outstanding balance will be satisfied in full at or prior to closing from the Borrower\u2019s own funds or from closing proceeds,\u201d and that the Company \u201chas not independently verified the outstanding balance\u201d; Credit Memorandum \u00a7 2.2 and \u00a7 9.7; Term Sheet \u00a7 18."),
 ("Discrepancy.", "The deed of trust from Foster Street Properties LLC (predecessor in title) to Triangle Commercial Bank, dated September 14, 2018, securing $3,400,000, is still of record. No payoff letter, balance statement, or cancellation is in the file. The Credit Memorandum says it will be paid at closing \u201cfrom the proceeds of the senior construction loan or from borrower funds,\u201d but the sources and uses contain no line item for it and the Borrower is contributing $0 in cash.  ("Impact.", "Closing cannot occur with a first-priority deed of trust until this lien is released.  ("Recommendation.", "Obtain a payoff letter dated within 30 days of closing, together with the underlying note and any modification or assumption documents (the Borrower\u2019s liability for the debt must be established: the deed is a special warranty deed and the Borrower may have taken subject to, rather than assuming, the lien). Escrow the payoff through the title company, record a cancellation in the form required by N.C.G.S. \u00a7 45-37, obtain a bring-down confirming recordation, and require the title policy to be issued without the exception. If a balance remains, add it to the uses and fund it with verified equity, and re-test LTC and LTV."),
 ("Where addressed.", "\u00a7 3.1(e) and \u00a7 13.2."),

issue("E-2", "The Term Sheet\u2019s four-item Permitted Exceptions list cannot be reconciled with the title commitment\u2019s thirteen exceptions", "Medium", [
 ("Sources.", "Term Sheet \u00a7 18 (four Permitted Exceptions; \u201call other exceptions shown on Schedule B-II \u2026 including but not limited to any prior deeds of trust, shall be removed, released, or otherwise satisfied\u201d); Title Commitment Schedule B-II (thirteen numbered exceptions plus special items); Credit Memorandum \u00a7 10.1.5 (\u201csubject only to approved standard title exceptions as determined by the Bank and its counsel\u201d)."),
 ("Discrepancy.", "Three of the title exceptions cannot be removed at all: 2025 ad valorem taxes not yet due (Item 7), the Unified Development Ordinance and MU-D zoning (Item 12), and parties in possession (Item 13, which can be deleted only with a survey and an affidavit of possession).  ("Impact.", "A title policy cannot be issued on the Term Sheet\u2019s terms, so the closing condition as written is impossible to satisfy, which invites a waiver at the closing table and a policy that does not match the loan documents."),
 ("Recommendation.", "Adopt Schedule 2 as drafted, which conforms the Permitted Exceptions to the title commitment, provides for deletion of the standard survey exceptions on delivery of the Survey and affidavits, preserves the mechanics\u2019 lien exception only with an ALTA 9 endorsement, and expressly carves out the Triangle Commercial Bank deed of trust and the environmental deed notice."),

issue("E-3", "Demolition and remediation work performed in August and September 2024 may prime the Bank\u2019s deed of trust under N.C.G.S. \u00a7 44A-10", "Critical", [
 ("Sources.", "Title Commitment Note 4 (mechanic\u2019s lien priority and the recommendation for owner and contractor affidavits); Phase I ESA \u00a7 1 and \u00a7 2.2 (demolition completed August 2024; remediation completed September 2024; pre-demolition hazardous materials survey by Southern Environmental Services Inc. in July 2024); Appraisal \u00a7 3 (the GMP contract \u201chas been executed and a copy was provided to the appraiser\u201d)."),
 ("Discrepancy.", "Neither the Term Sheet nor the Credit Memorandum addresses the fact that substantial work has already been performed on the Property. Under N.C.G.S. \u00a7 44A-10, a claim of lien relates back to the first furnishing of labor or materials, so claims by the demolition contractor, the remediation consultant, the hazardous materials surveyor, and any architect or engineer who performed pre-closing services could take priority over a deed of trust recorded at closing.  ("Impact.", "Loss of lien priority is not insurable except through specific title endorsements that require waivers and affidavits. If a pre-closing claimant perfects a lien, the Bank\u2019s collateral position is impaired and the title policy will not cover it."),
 ("Recommendation.", "As a condition of closing: (a) obtain unconditional lien waivers and releases from every person that has furnished labor, materials, or services, including the demolition contractor, Sentinel Environmental Consulting LLC, Southern Environmental Services Inc., and Architect; (b) obtain an owner\u2019s affidavit and a contractor\u2019s affidavit of no work performed and no materials furnished under the construction contract (or, if work has begun, full waivers and a title endorsement); (c) obtain an ALTA 9 endorsement and a pending-disbursement endorsement; and (d) covenant that no work will commence before the deed of trust is recorded."),
 ("Where addressed.", "\u00a7 3.1(r), \u00a7 13.4, and \u00a7 6.1(p)."),

 ("Recomputation.", "Parcel 1: 298.62\u2032 \u00d7 305.41\u2032 = 91,202 SF = 2.094 acres. Parcel 2: 201.88\u2032 \u00d7 297.63\u2032 = 60,086 SF = 1.379 acres.  ("Impact.", "The Phase I ESA\u2019s orientation and parcel descriptions are inconsistent with record title. issue("E-6", "The title commitment expires June 5, 2025 and the owner\u2019s policy amount and cost allocation are unconfirmed", "Low", [
 ("Sources.", "Title Commitment Note 1 (expiration six months after December 5, 2024); Schedule A (loan policy $47,500,000; owner\u2019s policy $8,900,000 to Borrower); Borrower\u2019s Detailed Budget line 3.07 (title insurance and recording $245,000 funded by the senior Loan)."),

 ("Recommendation.", "Obtain a payoff letter dated within 30 days of closing, together with the underlying note and any modification or assumption documents (the Borrower\u2019s liability for the debt must be established: the deed is a special warranty deed and the Borrower may have taken subject to, rather than assuming, the lien). Escrow the payoff through the title company, record a cancellation in the form required by N.C.G.S. \u00a7 45-37, obtain a bring-down confirming recordation, and require the title policy to be issued without the exception. If a balance remains, add it to the uses and fund it with verified equity, and re-test LTC and LTV."),
 ("Where addressed.", "\u00a7 3.1(e) and \u00a7 13.2."),
])

issue("E-2", "The Term Sheet\u2019s four-item Permitted Exceptions list cannot be reconciled with the title commitment\u2019s thirteen exceptions", "Medium", [
 ("Sources.", "Term Sheet \u00a7 18 (four Permitted Exceptions; \u201call other exceptions shown on Schedule B-II \u2026 including but not limited to any prior deeds of trust, shall be removed, released, or otherwise satisfied\u201d); Title Commitment Schedule B-II (thirteen numbered exceptions plus special items); Credit Memorandum \u00a7 10.1.5 (\u201csubject only to approved standard title exceptions as determined by the Bank and its counsel\u201d)."),
 ("Discrepancy.", "Three of the title exceptions cannot be removed at all: 2025 ad valorem taxes not yet due (Item 7), the Unified Development Ordinance and MU-D zoning (Item 12), and parties in possession (Item 13, which can be deleted only with a survey and an affidavit of possession). The Term Sheet does not list them, and it does not mention that the recorded environmental deed notice, once recorded, will also appear as an exception."),
 ("Impact.", "A title policy cannot be issued on the Term Sheet\u2019s terms, so the closing condition as written is impossible to satisfy, which invites a waiver at the closing table and a policy that does not match the loan documents."),
 ("Recommendation.", "Adopt Schedule 2 as drafted, which conforms the Permitted Exceptions to the title commitment, provides for deletion of the standard survey exceptions on delivery of the Survey and affidavits, preserves the mechanics\u2019 lien exception only with an ALTA 9 endorsement, and expressly carves out the Triangle Commercial Bank deed of trust and the environmental deed notice."),
 ("Where addressed.", "Schedule 2 and \u00a7 13.2."),
])

issue("E-3", "Demolition and remediation work performed in August and September 2024 may prime the Bank\u2019s deed of trust under N.C.G.S. \u00a7 44A-10", "Critical", [
 ("Sources.", "Title Commitment Note 4 (mechanic\u2019s lien priority and the recommendation for owner and contractor affidavits); Phase I ESA \u00a7 1 and \u00a7 2.2 (demolition completed August 2024; remediation completed September 2024; pre-demolition hazardous materials survey by Southern Environmental Services Inc. in July 2024); Appraisal \u00a7 3 (the GMP contract \u201chas been executed and a copy was provided to the appraiser\u201d)."),
 ("Discrepancy.", "Neither the Term Sheet nor the Credit Memorandum addresses the fact that substantial work has already been performed on the Property. Under N.C.G.S. \u00a7 44A-10, a claim of lien relates back to the first furnishing of labor or materials, so claims by the demolition contractor, the remediation consultant, the hazardous materials surveyor, and any architect or engineer who performed pre-closing services could take priority over a deed of trust recorded at closing. The Appraisal also indicates that the construction contract has already been executed, which raises the same issue for the contractor if it has mobilized or stored materials."),
 ("Impact.", "Loss of lien priority is not insurable except through specific title endorsements that require waivers and affidavits. If a pre-closing claimant perfects a lien, the Bank\u2019s collateral position is impaired and the title policy will not cover it."),
 ("Recommendation.", "As a condition of closing: (a) obtain unconditional lien waivers and releases from every person that has furnished labor, materials, or services, including the demolition contractor, Sentinel Environmental Consulting LLC, Southern Environmental Services Inc., and Architect; (b) obtain an owner\u2019s affidavit and a contractor\u2019s affidavit of no work performed and no materials furnished under the construction contract (or, if work has begun, full waivers and a title endorsement); (c) obtain an ALTA 9 endorsement and a pending-disbursement endorsement; and (d) covenant that no work will commence before the deed of trust is recorded."),
 ("Where addressed.", "\u00a7 3.1(r), \u00a7 13.4, and \u00a7 6.1(p)."),
])

issue("E-4", "Parcel acreage, site orientation, and street frontage differ across four documents", "Medium", [
 ("Sources.", "Title Commitment Schedule A \u00a7 6 (Parcel 1, 2.09 acres; Parcel 2, 1.38 acres; metes and bounds); Phase I ESA \u00a7 1, \u00a7 2.1 and Figure 3 (1.89 and 1.58 acres; \u201cthe site fronts Foster Street to the north\u201d; Parcel 2 described as the \u201ceastern parcel\u201d); Appraisal \u00a7 2 (\u201capproximately 420 feet of frontage along Foster Street on the western boundary\u201d; 3.47 acres / 151,153 square feet)."),
 ("Recomputation.", "Parcel 1: 298.62\u2032 \u00d7 305.41\u2032 = 91,202 SF = 2.094 acres. Parcel 2: 201.88\u2032 \u00d7 297.63\u2032 = 60,086 SF = 1.379 acres. Combined: 3.473 acres = 151,153 SF, which matches the Appraisal. The deeds also establish that Foster Street runs along the western boundary of both parcels (the first call of each description runs along \u201cthe eastern right-of-way margin of Foster Street\u201d), that Parcel 2 lies south of Parcel 1, and that combined frontage is 500.50 feet, not 420 feet."),
 ("Impact.", "The Phase I ESA\u2019s orientation and parcel descriptions are inconsistent with record title. Because the restriction is parcel- and area-specific, an administrator cannot determine which corner of which parcel is restricted, nor which units sit above it, until the delineation is re-plotted on a survey. The Appraisal\u2019s frontage figure is also wrong, although it does not affect value directly."),
 ("Recommendation.", "Require the ALTA/NSPS survey with the Table A items listed in \u00a7 13.5, including a boundary and acreage certification; require the surveyor\u2019s reconciliation of the deed acreage to the surveyed acreage; require the delineation overlay under \u00a7 10.5; and obtain a corrective letter from the consultant. Exhibit A to the draft uses the recorded descriptions and flags the discrepancy rather than adopting either set of acreage figures."),
 ("Where addressed.", "\u00a7 13.5, \u00a7 10.5, and Exhibit A."),
])

issue("E-5", "The Appraisal states that historic district architectural review approval has been obtained; the title officer reports no evidence of submission or approval", "Critical", [
 ("Sources.", "Appraisal \u00a7 2 (\u201cthe architectural design has been reviewed and approved by the Brightleaf Historic District Association in accordance with the CC&Rs\u201d); Title Commitment Schedule B-II Item 11 and the Title Officer\u2019s note (\u201cThe Company has not received evidence that the current project plans \u2026 have been submitted to or approved by the Brightleaf Historic District Association Architectural Review Committee\u201d); Credit Memorandum \u00a7 9.8 and \u00a7 10.1.14 (treat approval as outstanding)."),
 ("Discrepancy.", "A direct contradiction. The Declaration (recorded in Book 6984, Page 1155, as amended in Book 7102, Page 388) requires submission of all development plans to the Architectural Review Committee at least 90 days before construction, requires written approval (or deemed approval after 60 days of complete submission) as a condition to any building permit application, and gives the Association and any property owner the right to seek injunctive relief to stop unapproved construction."),
 ("Impact.", "If approval is not in place, the City can be expected to withhold the building permit and the Association can enjoin construction, which would be an immediate and expensive stoppage on a project whose construction maturity date already precedes its completion date. Reliance on the Appraisal\u2019s statement would be misplaced: the appraiser\u2019s scope did not include a title or covenant review."),
 ("Recommendation.", "Obtain a copy of the ARC approval letter, or a certificate of the Association that the 60-day deemed-approval period has run on a complete submission (with the submission date and the completeness determination documented). Also obtain an estoppel or letter from the Association confirming no default, no pending enforcement, and no unsatisfied conditions of approval, and confirm that no owner within the district has asserted an objection."),
 ("Where addressed.", "\u00a7 3.1(g), \u00a7 7.1(k), and \u00a7 8.1(h)."),
])

issue("E-6", "The title commitment expires June 5, 2025 and the owner\u2019s policy amount and cost allocation are unconfirmed", "Low", [
 ("Sources.", "Title Commitment Note 1 (expiration six months after December 5, 2024); Schedule A (loan policy $47,500,000; owner\u2019s policy $8,900,000 to Borrower); Borrower\u2019s Detailed Budget line 3.07 (title insurance and recording $245,000 funded by the senior Loan)."),
 ("Discrepancy.", "The commitment expires roughly three months after the target closing, which is adequate if closing occurs on time but not if it slips. The budget funds title premiums, including the owner\u2019s policy, from loan proceeds, although the Term Sheet obligates the Borrower to pay title costs (\u00a7 21.5) and the Loan Amount is the insured amount that matters to the Bank."),
 ("Recommendation.", "Require an extension or re-issuance if closing occurs after May 1, 2025. Confirm whether the Borrower intends to purchase an owner\u2019s policy at its own expense; if the premium is funded from loan proceeds it should appear as an identified budget line, and the Bank should not fund an owner\u2019s policy that benefits only the Borrower without Committee awareness."),
 ("Where addressed.", "Schedule 3, line 3.07; \u00a7 13.3."),
])
PYEOF
echo ok"}

tool_calls.name: bash
tool_calls.arguments:
{"command": "cd $WORKSPACE_DIR/build && cat >> build_memo.py <<'PYEOF'

h2(doc, "F.  Construction budget and draw schedule", size=11.5)
issue("F-1", "The Borrower\u2019s draw schedule does not withhold retainage, over-advances hard costs by $3,475,000, and contains four separate footing errors", "High", [
 ("Sources.", "Borrower\u2019s \u201cDraw Schedule\u201d tab, Section 1, dated January 8, 2025; Term Sheet \u00a7 9.1 (10% retainage on all hard cost disbursements, held by the Lender) and \u00a7 9.2 (Draw 9 \u201cRetainage Release\u201d $3,275,000); Credit Memorandum \u00a7 7.1 (\u201cThe retainage amount of $3,275,000 represents approximately 9.4% of the hard construction cost GMP\u201d)."),
 ("Discrepancy.", "The schedule presents four columns for each draw (gross hard cost, retainage, net, total draw), but the total draw for Draws 2 through 8 equals the gross amount in every case, so no retainage is actually withheld. Cumulative hard-cost funding is therefore $34,750,000 through Draw 8 plus a further $3,475,000 of \u201cretainage release\u201d at Draw 9 = $38,225,000 against a Guaranteed Maximum Price of $34,750,000: a $3,475,000 over-advance. Separately, the TOTAL row reports $47,500,000 although its cells sum to $48,500,000; the Developer Fee column cells sum to $923,750 against a stated $2,835,000; the Contingency column cells sum to $3,351,250 against a stated $1,440,000; the Retainage column cells sum to $(3,475,000) against a stated $0; and the Draw 9 row does not foot ($3,475,000 \u2212 $3,475,000 + $200,000 + $600,000 = $800,000 against a stated $3,275,000). Finally, the Term Sheet and the Credit Memorandum treat the retainage as 10% of the GMP ($3,475,000) but provide a release of $3,275,000, a $200,000 shortfall, and the Credit Memorandum rationalizes the difference by describing the release as 9.4% without noting the inconsistency."),
 ("Impact.", "The schedule, if used to fund the loan, would disburse $3,475,000 more for hard costs than the contract price supports, and would do so by relabeling retained funds as Developer Fee and Contingency within the same draw lines. That is the mechanism by which the appearance of reconciliation is achieved. The Borrower also cannot prepare a compliant draw request or an accurate budget reconciliation from a document that does not foot."),
 ("Recommendation.", "Do not approve the schedule. Require a corrected schedule before closing, and adopt the restated Schedule 4 to the Loan Agreement, which withholds 10% Retainage from each hard-cost advance, separates the Developer Fee (conditional, subordinate) and the Contingency (drawn only against approved change orders) from the Retainage Release, and reconciles to $47,500,000 of commitment with $34,750,000 of hard-cost funding. Require the Construction Inspector to reconcile every draw to the GMP schedule of values and to confirm that no amount allocable to retained work is being disbursed."),
 ("Where addressed.", "Schedule 4 (restated, with reconciliation table), \u00a7 5.3, \u00a7 5.8, and \u00a7 5.13."),
])
table(doc, [
    ["Draw", "Borrower\u2019s schedule: total draw", "Retainage actually withheld", "Restated: total advance", "Cumulative (restated)"],
    ["1 \u2014 Closing", "$9,475,000", "n/a", "$9,475,000", "$9,475,000"],
    ["2 through 8 \u2014 Hard costs", "$34,750,000", "$0", "$31,275,000", "$40,750,000"],
    ["9 \u2014 \u201cRetainage Release\u201d", "$3,275,000", "$(3,475,000) shown but re-advanced", "$3,475,000", "$44,225,000"],
    ["10 \u2014 Developer Fee", "embedded in Draws 6\u20139", "n/a", "$1,835,000", "$46,060,000"],
    ["11 \u2014 Contingency", "embedded in Draws 2\u20139", "n/a", "$1,440,000", "$47,500,000"],
    ["Total", "$47,500,000 (cells sum to $48,500,000)", "\u2014", "$47,500,000", "\u2014"],
], widths=[1.25, 1.5, 1.55, 1.0, 0.9], header=True, size=8, align_right_cols=(1, 3, 4), shade_last_row=True)

issue("F-2", "At least $1.7 million of required costs are not in the Approved Budget", "High", [
 ("Sources.", "Borrower\u2019s Detailed Budget (all tabs); Term Sheet \u00a7\u00a7 3.4 (exit fee and unused line fee), 21.5 (Borrower pays Lender\u2019s costs); Appraisal \u00a7 6.1 (demolition and remediation costs of approximately $680,000); Phase I ESA \u00a7 6.3 (remediation cost approximately $485,000); Title Commitment Schedule B-I Requirement 4 (Triangle Commercial Bank payoff)."),
 ("Recomputation.", "Unbudgeted items we can quantify: unused line fee of approximately $119,000 (0.25% per annum on an assumed average undrawn balance of $19,000,000 over 2.5 years); exit fee of $237,500 if repaid during construction or $118,750 if repaid in the first six months of the mini-perm; pre-closing demolition and remediation of approximately $680,000 (or $485,000 of remediation alone), which are Project costs incurred before closing and outside the budget; and the interest reserve shortfall of $365,830 to $565,000 (Issue H-1). Items we cannot quantify from the record: the Triangle Commercial Bank payoff, retail tenant improvements (line 2.07 is core and shell only), and leasing commissions."),
 ("Impact.", "Each of these is a cost the Borrower must pay. With zero cash equity, each becomes either an overrun funded by the guarantors or an unfunded obligation that impairs completion. The pre-closing costs also bear on whether the stated Total Project Cost of $56,700,000 is a true all-in cost."),
 ("Recommendation.", "Add the quantifiable items to Total Project Costs, fund them with verified equity, and update the sources and uses. As noted in Issue A-1, this both cures the LTC breach and funds the reserve shortfall. Require the Borrower to confirm in writing that the budget is complete and that no material cost is omitted."),
 ("Where addressed.", "Schedule 3 (note identifying omitted costs) and \u00a7 9.1 (Total Project Costs defined to include actually incurred costs)."),
])

issue("F-3", "The contingency is 3.28% of hard costs for a 30-month wood-frame project in a historic district", "Medium", [
 ("Sources.", "Borrower\u2019s Detailed Budget lines 6.01\u20136.02 ($1,140,000 hard cost contingency; $300,000 soft cost contingency); Credit Memorandum \u00a7 5.2 (describes the total $1,440,000 as \u201capproximately 4.1% of hard construction costs\u201d); Appraisal \u00a7 3 (Type III-A wood-frame superstructure over a reinforced concrete podium on driven piles)."),
 ("Discrepancy.", "The $1,440,000 total is 4.14% of hard costs only if the soft cost component is counted against hard costs. Measured properly, the hard cost contingency is 3.28% and the soft cost contingency is 7.23% of soft costs. The Credit Memorandum\u2019s presentation blends the two and overstates hard cost coverage."),
 ("Impact.", "Wood-frame construction over a podium on driven piles, in a historic district subject to architectural review, is a higher-change-order profile than the 3.3% contingency implies. An underfunded contingency becomes a guarantor obligation."),
 ("Recommendation.", "Confirm with the Borrower and Contractor that no change orders are pending or anticipated and that the GMP includes all site conditions; consider increasing the hard cost contingency to 5% ($1,737,500, an increase of $297,500) funded by equity, which further improves LTC under Issue A-1 option (2)."),
 ("Where addressed.", "Schedule 3, lines 6.01\u20136.02; \u00a7 5.6 (overruns) and \u00a7 5.7 (change orders)."),
])

issue("F-4", "The Loan is described as a \u201csingle advance facility,\u201d funded in nine draws, with an unused line fee", "Medium", [
 ("Sources.", "Term Sheet \u00a7 3.1 (\u201cstructured as a single advance facility, with loan proceeds to be disbursed in accordance with the approved draw schedule\u201d), \u00a7 3.4 (unused line fee of 0.25% on the average daily undrawn commitment) and \u00a7 9.2 (nine milestone draws); Credit Memorandum \u00a7 4.1."),
 ("Discrepancy.", "The three provisions describe different facilities: a single-advance loan has no undrawn commitment and no milestone draws; an unused line fee is a revolving-credit concept."),
 ("Impact.", "Ambiguity in the fee basis and in whether undrawn amounts must be advanced on demand."),
 ("Recommendation.", "Confirm with the Committee whether the unused line fee is intended. The draft treats the commitment as non-revolving, advances in milestone draws, and preserves the fee on the average undrawn commitment (\u00a7 2.2). If the fee is not intended, delete \u00a7 2.6(c) and confirm the deletion in the credit approval, since the fee is not in the Approved Budget either way (Issue F-2)."),
 ("Where addressed.", "\u00a7 2.2 and \u00a7 2.6(c)."),
])

issue("F-5", "Draw 1 equals 20% of the commitment at 0% completion and funds the Bank\u2019s own transaction costs", "Medium", [
 ("Sources.", "Term Sheet \u00a7 9.2 (Draw 1 $9,475,000 at 0% complete); Borrower\u2019s Detailed Budget lines 3.04 (lender legal and title $310,000) and 3.07 (title and recording $245,000), funded by the senior Loan."),
 ("Recomputation.", "Draw 1 is $9,475,000 of the $47,500,000 commitment, or 19.95%, advanced before any work is performed, comprising soft costs of $4,150,000 (of which $555,000 is the Bank\u2019s own legal and title cost), the interest reserve of $4,850,000, and the origination fee of $475,000. On an all-in construction rate of 6.75%, Draw 1 alone accrues approximately $53,300 of interest per month."),
 ("Impact.", "The front-loaded draw raises the average outstanding balance above a linear assumption and therefore raises the interest cost, which is part of why the reserve analysis is sensitive to the draw curve."),
 ("Recommendation.", "Accept the structure as consistent with the Term Sheet, but consider escrowing the soft cost portion and reimbursing against invoices, and require the Borrower to pay its own transactional costs from equity rather than financing the Bank\u2019s fees. If that change is made, the interest reserve requirement decreases correspondingly."),
 ("Where addressed.", "\u00a7 5.1 and Schedule 4, Draw 1."),
])

issue("F-6", "The GMP contract is reported as already executed, although its execution is also a closing condition", "High", [
 ("Sources.", "Appraisal \u00a7 3 (\u201cThe GMP contract has been executed and a copy was provided to the appraiser for review\u201d); Term Sheet \u00a7 11 and Credit Memorandum \u00a7 10.1.8 (execution and delivery of the construction contract as a condition precedent); Borrower\u2019s Detailed Budget line 2.01 (site work including demolition, which has already occurred)."),
 ("Discrepancy.", "If the contract is executed, the closing condition is either already satisfied or was never unmet; more importantly, execution may mean mobilization, procurement, or stored materials, which compounds the lien relation-back problem in Issue E-3."),
 ("Impact.", "The Bank does not know whether work has commenced or costs have been incurred under a contract it has not seen, approved, or received by collateral assignment."),
 ("Recommendation.", "Obtain the fully executed contract with all exhibits and the schedule of values, confirm the execution date and the status of any work, materials, or long-lead procurement, and condition closing on delivery of the collateral assignment, the contractor\u2019s consent, and the waivers described in Issue E-3."),
 ("Where addressed.", "\u00a7 3.1(l) and \u00a7 13.4."),
])

issue("F-7", "No payment or performance bonds are required anywhere in the record", "Medium", [
 ("Sources.", "Term Sheet \u00a7\u00a7 8 and 11 (collateral assignment of the construction contract; no bond requirement); Credit Memorandum \u00a7 9.8 (recommends verifying the contractor\u2019s \u201cfinancial strength and payment and performance bonding capacity\u201d but does not require bonds)."),
 ("Discrepancy.", "A $34,750,000 GMP contract with a single general contractor is the principal construction risk in the transaction, and the record contains no bonding requirement and no contractor financial information."),
 ("Impact.", "If the contractor fails, the completion guaranty bears the entire burden of completing the work, and the guarantors\u2019 net worth is the Bank\u2019s only recourse."),
 ("Recommendation.", "Require payment and performance bonds in the full GMP amount, naming the Bank as dual obligee, issued by a surety rated A- VIII or better, and require the contractor\u2019s most recent audited financial statements, a current balance sheet, and evidence of aggregate bonding capacity (\u00a7 5.10)."),
 ("Where addressed.", "\u00a7 5.10 and Schedule 6."),
])

h2(doc, "G.  Schedule and covenant mechanics", size=11.5)
issue("G-1", "The construction maturity date precedes the projected substantial completion date by three days", "High", [
 ("Sources.", "Term Sheet \u00a7 3.2 (Construction Maturity Date August 28, 2027, being 30 months from a February 28, 2025 closing) and \u00a7 7.1 (Completion Guaranty requires completion \u201con or before the Construction Maturity Date of August 28, 2027\u201d); Term Sheet \u00a7 2 and Appraisal \u00a7 3 (projected substantial completion August 31, 2027); Credit Memorandum \u00a7 9.6 (identifies the three-day gap but treats it as a matter for mitigation)."),
 ("Discrepancy.", "The Project\u2019s own schedule completes after the date on which the loan matures and after which the Completion Guaranty requires completion. The Borrower\u2019s draw schedule places the substantial completion draw in August 2027 and the retainage release in October 2027, after maturity."),
 ("Impact.", "The Completion Guaranty is breached at inception on the Project\u2019s own schedule, and any delay of even one day produces a maturity default during the period in which the mini-perm is supposed to provide a buffer. A guaranty that is in default before construction begins is of little value and invites litigation over whether the guarantors were ever obligated."),
 ("Recommendation.", "Conform the documents. Either extend the Construction Period so that the Construction Maturity Date is not earlier than the projected substantial completion date plus a realistic contingency (we suggest November 30, 2027, or 33 months from closing), or state the guaranteed completion date as the later of the Construction Maturity Date and the approved baseline schedule completion date. Do not close with a Completion Guaranty that the Project\u2019s own schedule cannot satisfy."),
 ("Where addressed.", "\u00a7 14.1 (with a conforming paragraph) and \u00a7 1.1 (Construction Maturity Date)."),
])

issue("G-2", "The DSCR covenant cannot be tested as written at the start of the mini-perm period", "High", [
 ("Sources.", "Term Sheet \u00a7 6.3 (\u201ctested at the commencement of the Mini-Perm Period and annually thereafter based on actual trailing twelve-month net operating income\u201d); Credit Memorandum \u00a7 6.1 and \u00a7 11(c); Appraisal \u00a7 6.3 (stabilization projected for approximately May 2028); Term Sheet \u00a7 2 (substantial completion August 31, 2027)."),
 ("Discrepancy.", "The mini-perm period begins August 29, 2027, immediately after construction completion. There is no trailing twelve-month operating history, and the Appraisal does not project stabilization until May 2028. A literal application of the covenant produces a DSCR of zero and an Event of Default on the first day of the mini-perm period."),
 ("Impact.", "An automatic default at the moment the construction period ends is the worst possible timing: it converts the intended buffer into a trigger and would permit the Bank to accelerate at the point where the Borrower most needs the mini-perm to perform."),
 ("Recommendation.", "Test on a projected basis at the commencement of the mini-perm period, using projected stabilized NOI and interest-only debt service at the then-current rate, and perform the first actual trailing twelve-month test at the end of the twelfth full month after the final certificate of occupancy (drafted). Consider a lower interim threshold during lease-up (for example 1.15x) with a cash sweep or cash management trigger."),
 ("Where addressed.", "\u00a7 9.3 and Schedule 5."),
])

issue("G-3", "Stressed coverage is 1.04x and an interest rate cap is required only if the extension is exercised", "High", [
 ("Sources.", "Credit Memorandum \u00a7 6.1 (stressed DSCR 1.04x at a 9.85% rate) and \u00a7 11(f) (cap required as a condition of the extension only); Term Sheet \u00a7 3.2 (extension option)."),
 ("Discrepancy.", "A 200-basis-point increase in SOFR takes coverage to 1.04x, below the 1.25x minimum, and the Loan is a floating-rate facility for its entire term. Protection is required only at the extension, which is 18 months after the construction maturity date."),
 ("Impact.", "The Borrower may be unable to refinance at mini-perm maturity precisely because of rate movement, which is the risk the mini-perm period is intended to bridge."),
 ("Recommendation.", "Require an interest rate cap from the commencement of the mini-perm period (not only on extension), with a strike at or about the then-current rate plus 200 basis points, from a counterparty rated A- or better, collaterally assigned to the Bank (drafted for extension; extend to mini-perm commencement)."),
 ("Where addressed.", "\u00a7 7.1(n) and \u00a7 22.1(6)."),
])

issue("G-4", "The construction delay default is measured against a schedule that has not been delivered", "Medium", [
 ("Sources.", "Term Sheet \u00a7 15 (\u201cConstruction Delay Default shall be deemed to occur if the Project is more than ninety (90) days behind the approved construction schedule\u201d); Credit Memorandum \u00a7 7.2 (schedule updates required monthly)."),
 ("Discrepancy.", "No construction schedule is in the record, and no provision makes the delivery and approval of a baseline schedule a closing condition. The milestone draw schedule in \u00a7 9.2 of the Term Sheet is a funding schedule, not a critical path schedule."),
 ("Impact.", "The delay default is unenforceable without a baseline."),
 ("Recommendation.", "Require delivery and Bank approval of a baseline CPM schedule at closing, attach it as a schedule to the Loan Agreement, and measure the 90-day threshold against it."),
 ("Where addressed.", "\u00a7 15.1(g) and \u00a7 3.1."),
])

h2(doc, "H.  Interest reserve", size=11.5)
issue("H-1", "The two interest reserve analyses disagree, and the Borrower\u2019s conclusion depends on a SOFR assumption 85 basis points below the rate used in the credit approval", "High", [
 ("Sources.", "Term Sheet \u00a7 10 and \u00a7 5.2 ($4,850,000 reserve); Credit Memorandum \u00a7 6.2 (shortfall of approximately $565,000; at +100 bps, approximately $1,278,000); Borrower\u2019s \u201cDraw Schedule\u201d tab, Section 2 (SOFR assumed at 3.50%; total interest $4,628,675; surplus $221,325; concluded \u201cAPPEARS ADEQUATE\u201d), and its own sensitivity table (at 4.35% SOFR: total interest $5,215,830, shortfall $365,830)."),
 ("Recomputation.", "The Bank\u2019s methodology (average balance of $28,500,000 \u00d7 7.60% \u00d7 2.5 years) produces $5,415,000 of interest and a $565,000 shortfall. The Borrower\u2019s draw-by-draw model, run at the same 7.60% rate, produces $5,215,830 and a $365,830 shortfall. The $199,170 difference is attributable to methodology (flat average balance versus a month-by-month balance curve), not to any dispute about rates. Both conclusions contradict the Borrower\u2019s headline result, which assumes 3.50% SOFR rather than the 4.35% current rate that the Credit Memorandum itself uses."),
 ("Impact.", "On the Bank\u2019s own analysis the reserve is short by between $366,000 and $565,000 at today\u2019s rate, and by approximately $1,278,000 at a rate 100 basis points higher. With zero cash equity (Issue A-3), a shortfall becomes a payment default during construction, a cross-default under the mezzanine loan, and a guarantor call."),
 ("Recommendation.", "Adopt a single methodology: the draw-based model at the greater of the current SOFR and 4.35%, tested at each draw against projected costs through the earlier of the next draw and 90 days (drafted). Size the reserve to the higher of the two estimates plus a cushion \u2014 approximately $5,600,000, an increase of $750,000 \u2014 and fund the increase with verified equity, which also improves LTC under Issue A-1 option (2). Retain the hard replenishment covenant (five Business Days) and make failure to fund a shortfall an immediate Event of Default. Do not accept a reserve analysis that depends on a rate 85 basis points below current market."),
 ("Where addressed.", "\u00a7 5.5 (a) through (f), Exhibit D (adequacy certificate), and Schedule 3, line 4.01."),
])
PYEOF
echo ok"}

issue("F-5", "Draw 1 equals 20% of the commitment at 0% completion and funds the Bank\u2019s own transaction costs", "Medium", [
 ("Sources.", "Term Sheet \u00a7 9.2 (Draw 1 $9,475,000 at 0% complete); Borrower\u2019s Detailed Budget lines 3.04 (lender legal and title $310,000) and 3.07 (title and recording $245,000), funded by the senior Loan."),

 ("Sources.", "Term Sheet \u00a7 6.3 (\u201ctested at the commencement of the Mini-Perm Period and annually thereafter based on actual trailing twelve-month net operating income\u201d); Credit Memorandum \u00a7 6.1 and \u00a7 11(c); Appraisal \u00a7 6.3 (stabilization projected for approximately May 2028); Term Sheet \u00a7 2 (substantial completion August 31, 2027)."),

The Borrower\u2019s draw-by-draw model, run at the same 7.60% rate, produces $5,215,830 and a $365,830 shortfall. Retain the hard replenishment covenant (five Business Days) and make failure to fund a shortfall an immediate Event of Default. Do not accept a reserve analysis that depends on a rate 85 basis points below current market."),

{"command": "cd $WORKSPACE_DIR/build && cat >> build_memo.py <<'PYEOF'

h2(doc, "I.  Insurance", size=11.5)
issue("I-1", "Builder\u2019s risk is required only in the amount of the hard costs, while the completed improvements are worth $56.7 million to $72.8 million", "High", [
 ("Sources.", "Term Sheet \u00a7 19 and \u00a7 11, and Credit Memorandum \u00a7 8.1 (\u201cIn an amount not less than the total hard construction costs ($34,750,000), on an all-risk, replacement cost basis\u201d); Appraisal \u00a7 10 (as-completed value $72,800,000; $253.22 per square foot of gross building area); Borrower\u2019s Detailed Budget line 3.09 (builder\u2019s risk premium $210,000)."),
 ("Discrepancy.", "The requirement is internally contradictory: an all-risk policy on a replacement cost basis must insure the replacement cost of the improvements, which includes soft costs, fees, and the developer\u2019s profit, not merely the hard cost contract price. Total Project Costs are $56,700,000 and the as-completed value is $72,800,000, so insuring to $34,750,000 leaves between $22 million and $38 million uninsured and, if the policy contains a coinsurance clause, imports a penalty on every partial loss."),
 ("Impact.", "An uninsured or underinsured casualty during construction is the classic construction-lender loss: the collateral is destroyed, the loan is not repaid, and the guarantors are asked to fund a rebuild they did not insure."),
 ("Recommendation.", "Require builder\u2019s risk in an amount not less than the full replacement cost of the completed improvements (not less than $56,700,000 in any event), including soft costs, with a coinsurance waiver, an agreed-amount endorsement, and a deductible not exceeding $25,000 without the Bank\u2019s consent (drafted)."),
 ("Where addressed.", "\u00a7 12.1(a) and Schedule 6."),
])

issue("I-2", "There is no property or rental loss insurance requirement for the twelve-month mini-perm period", "High", [
 ("Sources.", "Term Sheet \u00a7 19 (coverages listed: builder\u2019s risk, commercial general liability, umbrella, workers\u2019 compensation, and \u201csuch other insurance\u201d); Credit Memorandum \u00a7 8.1 (same)."),
 ("Discrepancy.", "Builder\u2019s risk covers the construction period. Nothing in the record requires permanent property insurance or business income and rental loss insurance once the building is complete, which is precisely when the Bank is relying on leases for repayment."),
 ("Impact.", "A casualty in the first year of operation could eliminate the income stream that services the Loan, in a period when there is no equity cushion to absorb the interruption."),
 ("Recommendation.", "Require, from substantial completion through maturity, special-form property insurance at full insurable value and business income and rental loss insurance covering not less than twelve months of NOI and continuing expenses, both naming the Bank as mortgagee and loss payee (drafted)."),
 ("Where addressed.", "\u00a7 12.1(e) and Schedule 6."),
])

issue("I-3", "Architect\u2019s professional liability and contractor\u2019s pollution coverage are not required in the Term Sheet, and the flood zone panel identification conflicts", "Medium", [
 ("Sources.", "Term Sheet \u00a7 19 (no professional liability or pollution coverage); Credit Memorandum \u00a7 8.1 (architect\u2019s E&O of $2,000,000, omitted from the Term Sheet); Phase I ESA \u00a7 2.3 (Zone X, FIRM panel 3720098700J, effective March 2, 2009); Appraisal \u00a7 2 (Zone X, panel 3710406400J, effective May 2, 2019)."),
 ("Discrepancy.", "The Bank is taking a collateral assignment of the architect\u2019s agreement and the plans but does not require the architect to carry professional liability insurance, and it is financing work in a contaminated area without contractor pollution coverage. The two documents agree on Zone X but cite different FIRM panels and effective dates, so at least one is stale."),
 ("Impact.", "Design defects and pollution incidents during the restricted area work would be uninsured."),
 ("Recommendation.", "Require architect\u2019s E&O of not less than $2,000,000 for the term plus three years, and contractor\u2019s pollution liability of not less than $2,000,000 for the restricted area work. Obtain a current flood zone determination from a recognized vendor and confirm that no portion of the Property is in a Special Flood Hazard Area (if it is, flood insurance is mandatory under the Bank\u2019s regulatory obligations)."),
 ("Where addressed.", "\u00a7 12.1(f) and (g) and Schedule 6."),
])

h2(doc, "J.  Legal and enforceability issues", size=11.5)
issue("J-1", "The Credit Memorandum mischaracterizes North Carolina foreclosure law", "Medium", [
 ("Sources.", "Credit Memorandum \u00a7 4.3 (\u201cNorth Carolina is a judicial foreclosure state and \u2026 deficiency judgments following foreclosure are subject to the fair price confirmation hearing requirements of N.C.G.S. \u00a7 45-21.36\u201d); Term Sheet \u00a7 16 (foreclosure \u201cin accordance with the laws of the State of North Carolina\u201d)."),
 ("Discrepancy.", "North Carolina deeds of trust are ordinarily enforced by a non-judicial power-of-sale proceeding conducted before the clerk of superior court under Article 2A of Chapter 45 of the North Carolina General Statutes (N.C.G.S. \u00a7\u00a7 45-21.1 through 45-21.33). A deficiency is pursued in a separate civil action and is limited by the fair-price provisions of N.C.G.S. \u00a7 45-21.36, which permit the court to credit the debtor with the fair market value of the property where the foreclosure price was inadequate. The credit approval\u2019s premise \u2014 that a judicial foreclosure with fair-price confirmation is the primary remedy \u2014 is incorrect."),
 ("Impact.", "The error matters to three things the credit approval relies on: the speed of the Bank\u2019s remedy (a power-of-sale foreclosure is faster than a judicial action), the enforceability of the guaranties (which are separate obligations and are not limited by the anti-deficiency framework, subject to the fair-price credit on any deficiency), and the structure of any springing full-recourse carve-out."),
 ("Recommendation.", "Correct the credit memorandum and confirm with North Carolina counsel that (a) the deed of trust contains a valid power of sale and appoints a trustee, (b) the guaranties are enforceable as independent obligations with the waivers drafted (including waiver of the right to require the Bank to pursue the collateral first), and (c) the Bank\u2019s election of remedies is preserved. The draft provides for both power-of-sale and judicial foreclosure alternatives and for a deficiency action subject to \u00a7 45-21.36 (\u00a7 16.1(4))."),
 ("Where addressed.", "Article 16 and \u00a7 14.5."),
])

issue("J-2", "The \u201cbad boy\u201d full-recourse trigger for a voluntary bankruptcy filing is controlled by an affiliate of the mezzanine lender", "Medium", [
 ("Sources.", "Term Sheet \u00a7 7.3 (full-recourse carve-outs including \u201cvoluntary bankruptcy\u201d); Credit Memorandum \u00a7 9.3 (independent manager as the safeguard against a bad-faith filing); Organizational Chart \u00a7 2.2 (75% member approval required for a voluntary bankruptcy filing, with Brightleaf Investors Group LLC holding the swing vote)."),
 ("Discrepancy.", "The most valuable recourse trigger in the guaranty package can only be activated by a filing that requires the consent of the affiliate of the subordinate lender. Either the Borrower cannot file voluntarily at all (which is protective, but not for the reason the documents assume), or it files only with that affiliate\u2019s consent, in which case the Bank\u2019s full-recourse remedy depends on a third party\u2019s decision."),
